definition_zh: 语言学家；（宽泛地）通晓多种语言的人
definition_en: a person who studies language scientifically, or more loosely a person who knows several languages
core_image: 一位研究者坐在野外折叠椅上，膝上放着录音笔与写满记号的笔记本，面前的老人正对着麦克风说话
scene: 野外的折叠椅上坐着一位研究者，膝上放着录音笔与写满记号的笔记本。The linguist spent three seasons recording a language with fewer than forty speakers.
sceneCN: 这里指「以科学方法研究语言的人」（第 1 个义项：语言研究者）；句意为这位研究者用了三个季节，记录一种使用者不足四十人的语言。可辨识物件：折叠椅、录音笔、笔记本、麦克风。

pos.zh: 语言学家；通晓多种语言的人（可数）

senses.title: A scientific student of language
senses.titleCN: 以科学方法研究语言的人
senses.definition: a person who studies the structure, history or use of language as a researcher
senses.definitionCN: 以研究者身份研究语言结构、历史或使用的人
senses.example: The linguist argued that no dialect is grammatically inferior.
senses.exampleCN: 这位语言学家主张，没有哪种方言在语法上更低劣。
senses.why: the word began as a name for someone skilled in languages and was narrowed to the scientific sense in the nineteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指精通语言的人，十九世纪才收窄为科学研究者的意思。

senses.title: A specialist in one language or family
senses.titleCN: 某一语言或语系的专家
senses.definition: a scholar whose expertise is a particular language, family or region
senses.definitionCN: 专长于某一语言、语系或地区的学者
senses.example: A specialist in the family identified the inscription within a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一位熟悉该语系的专家一天之内就辨认出这段铭文。
senses.why: specialization is the everyday form that the general title takes inside universities.
senses.whyCN: 在大学内部，这个通称最常见的形态就是「专精某一领域」。

senses.title: A person who knows many languages
senses.definition: a loose everyday use for someone fluent in several languages
senses.definitionCN: 日常宽泛用法，指能流利使用多种语言的人
senses.example: He was a fine linguist, at ease in six or seven languages.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位出色的语言通，六七种语言都说得自在。
senses.why: the older sense survives because knowing many tongues was once the clearest proof of skill with language.
senses.whyCN: 旧义仍然留存，因为通晓多语曾是语言能力最明显的证明。

senses.title: A historical linguist
senses.definition: a researcher who reconstructs how languages changed and split in the past
senses.definitionCN: 重构语言过去如何变化与分化的研究者
senses.example: The historical linguist traced the word back to an older root.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史语言学家把这个词追到一个更古老的词根。
senses.why: reconstructing the past is a distinct craft inside the field, and its practitioners keep the general title.
senses.whyCN: 重构过去是学科内一门独立技艺，其从业者沿用通称。

senses.title: A descriptive field worker
senses.titleCN: 做田野描写的语言调查者
senses.definition: a researcher who records a language by working with its speakers
senses.definitionCN: 通过与使用者合作来记录一种语言的研究者
senses.example: Field linguists wrote down songs no outsider had heard.
senses.exampleCN: 田野语言学家记录下外来者从未听过的歌。
senses.why: the discipline needed people to go where the language was spoken, and the title went with them.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科需要有人到说这种语言的地方去，这个称号也随之而去。

senses.title: A computational linguist
senses.definition: a researcher who builds computational models of language
senses.definitionCN: 建立语言计算模型的研究者
senses.example: The computational linguist trained the parser on a new corpus.
senses.exampleCN: 这位计算语言学家在新的语料上训练句法分析器。
senses.why: the field's models had to be implementable, which created a new kind of practitioner.
senses.whyCN: 学科的模型必须可实现，于是产生了一类新的从业者。

senses.title: An applied linguist
senses.definition: a researcher who applies linguistic findings to teaching, medicine or policy
senses.definitionCN: 把语言学成果用于教学、医疗或政策的研究者
senses.example: An applied linguist redesigned the reading test.
senses.exampleCN: 一位应用语言学家重新设计了阅读测试。
senses.why: findings had to travel into classrooms and clinics, so applied work acquired the title.
senses.whyCN: 研究成果必须进入课堂与诊所，应用工作因此获得了这个称号。

senses.title: A forensic linguist
senses.definition: a specialist who analyses wording as evidence in legal cases
senses.definitionCN: 在法律案件中把措辞当作证据分析的专家
senses.example: The forensic linguist compared the ransom note with the suspect's letters.
senses.exampleCN: 司法语言学家把勒索信与嫌疑人的书信作了比对。
senses.why: courts needed a reader of wording, and the discipline supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要有人读懂措辞，学科便提供了这样的人。

intro.en: Linguist comes from Latin lingua 'tongue, language' plus the person-ending -ista, probably through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加表人的词尾，很可能经法语传入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'. Its deeper origin is unsettled and no older form is attested.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」，更深来源无定论，也没有更早形式的书证。

items.en: The ending -ista named a person concerned with something, and passed into French and English as a marker of occupation or skill.
items.cn: 表人的词尾指从事某事的人，经法语与英语成为职业或技能的标记。

items.en: In the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries a linguist was simply someone skilled in languages, often a traveller or a clergyman.
items.cn: 在十七与十八世纪，这个词只指精通语言的人，常是旅行者或神职人员。

items.en: Nineteenth-century comparative philology gave the word its modern academic meaning, the student of language as a science.
items.cn: 十九世纪的比较语文学赋予它现代学术含义，即把语言作为科学来研究的人。

items.en: The twentieth century produced historical, field, computational, applied and forensic linguists as the field divided its labour.
items.cn: 二十世纪随着学科分工，出现了历史、田野、计算、应用与司法语言学家等称号。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root is unknown, and the first English use of the scientific sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语之前的词根不明，这个科学义在英语中最早使用的年代只能约略推定。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that are easily mistaken for the person; group two holds people described by their command of languages.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、容易被误当作「人」的词形；第二组是以语言能力来描述的人。

entries.definition: The discipline, not a person in it; a linguist works inside linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科，而非学科中的人；语言学家在语言学内部工作。

entries.definition: Describes what relates to language; it cannot name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与语言有关的性质，不能指人。

entries.definition: The system under study; a linguist studies language but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 指被研究的系统；语言学家研究语言，但本身不是语言。

entries.definition: A scholar of texts and languages in the older tradition, close but not identical to a linguist.
entries.definitionCN: 旧传统中研究文本与语言的学者，与语言学家接近但不相同。

entries.definition: A person who speaks many languages; the emphasis is on use, not research.
entries.definitionCN: 指会说多种语言的人，重点在使用，而非研究。

entries.definition: A person who turns writing from one language into another; skill in languages is a tool, not a science.
entries.definitionCN: 指把文字从一种语言转换为另一种的人；语言能力是工具，不是科学。

entries.definition: A person who renders speech live between languages, a practical rather than academic role.
entries.definitionCN: 指现场口译的人，属实务而非学术角色。

entries.definition: A specialist in word origins, a narrow branch of linguistic work.
entries.definitionCN: 指专研词源的学者，是语言工作中较窄的一支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means tongue, and the ending marks a person, so the word is literally a tongue-person.
normal.cn: 词根意为「舌头」，词尾标记人，因此这个词字面上就是「摆弄舌头的人」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases add the specialty: field, historical, computational, forensic.
normal.cn: 固定搭配补上专长：田野、历史、计算、司法。

normal.en: The everyday sense of a multilingual person is older than the academic sense.
normal.cn: 「会说多语的人」这一日常义，比学术义更古老。

normal.en: The family runs language, linguistic, linguistics, bilingual, multilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言」「语言的」「语言学」「双语的」「多语的」。

normal.en: The plural simply adds one ending, so counts of researchers are easy to form.
normal.cn: 复数只加一个词尾，统计研究者人数很容易。

abstract.en: Picture a person with a notebook in a village where only a few old speakers remain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人带着笔记本，走进只剩几位年长说话者的村子。

abstract.en: Picture a tongue turned into a measuring instrument.
abstract.cn: 想象舌头被改造成一件测量工具。

abstract.en: Picture a detective who reads wording instead of footprints.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读措辞而不读脚印的侦探。

examples.en: The linguist published a grammar of a language with no written tradition.
examples.cn: 这位语言学家出版了一种没有书写传统语言的语法。

examples.en: A good linguist listens before proposing a rule.
examples.cn: 好的语言学家先倾听，再提出规则。

examples.en: The court hired a linguist to compare the two letters.
examples.cn: 法庭聘请了一位语言学家来比对这两封信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林归斯特」——把林子里的方言归拢起来研究的那个人，就是语言学家。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加表人的词尾，经法语进入英语；早期指精通语言的人，十九世纪比较语文学兴起后收窄为以科学方法研究语言的人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one person from several directions: the researcher, the specialist, the multilingual, then the historical, field, computational, applied and forensic versions of the role.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从多个方向描述同一个人：研究者、专精者、通晓多语者，然后是历史、田野、计算、应用与司法等不同版本的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folding chair in the field, a recorder, and a notebook full of marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：野外的折叠椅、录音笔，以及写满记号的笔记本。

branches.en: THE CORE ROLE: a scientific student of language is the modern centre of the word.
branches.cn: 核心角色：以科学方法研究语言的人，是这个词的现代中心。

branches.en: NARROW EXPERTISE: universities turn the general title into specialists in one family.
branches.cn: 狭窄专长：大学把这个通称变成某一语系的专家。

branches.en: THE OLDER SENSE: knowing many languages still counts as being a linguist in ordinary speech.
branches.cn: 较旧的含义：在日常说法里，通晓多语仍算语言学家。

branches.en: PAST AND PRESENT SPEAKERS: some reconstruct history, others record living speech.
branches.cn: 过去的与现在的说话者：有人重构历史，有人记录活的语言。

branches.en: WORKING ROLES: machines, classrooms and courtrooms each employ the title.
branches.cn: 工作中的角色：机器、课堂与法庭各自雇用这个称号。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root plus a person-ending, and the same root builds the whole family of language terms.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加表人的词尾构成，同一词根也构成整套「语言」术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives the root, and the person-ending entered English through French; the same pair builds names for practitioners in many fields.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 提供词根，表人的词尾经法语进入英语；同一组合也为许多领域的从业者造名。

items.example: The root names the object the person works on.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指此人所研究的对象。

items.example: The ending turns a field into a person who works in it.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把领域变成在其中工作的人。

items.example: Language is what the linguist studies.
items.exampleCN: 语言是语言学家研究的东西。

items.example: Linguistic evidence supported the claim.
items.exampleCN: 语言证据支持了这一主张。

items.example: Linguistics trains new linguists.
items.exampleCN: 语言学培养新的语言学家。

items.example: A bilingual informant checked the translation.
items.exampleCN: 一位双语发音人核对了译文。

items.example: Multilingual editors joined the project.
The trade lingo puzzled the new apprentice.
items.exampleCN: 行业行话让新学徒摸不着头脑。

definition_zh: 语言的；语言学的；与语言运用有关的
definition_en: relating to language or to the scientific study of language
core_image: 一页写满分句与箭头的手稿，句子之间用细线连起，页边标着几个小号数
scene: 书桌上摊着一页写满分句与箭头的手稿，句子之间用细线相连。The editors examined linguistic clues before they dated the manuscript.
sceneCN: 这里指「与语言特征有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及语言本身的）；句意为编者在为手稿定年之前，先检查了语言线索。可辨识物件：手稿、分句、箭头、细线。

pos.zh: 语言的；语言学的

senses.title: Relating to language itself
senses.definition: concerning the sounds, words and grammar of a language
senses.definitionCN: 涉及一种语言的声音、词汇与语法
senses.example: Linguistic change is usually gradual rather than sudden.
senses.exampleCN: 语言变化通常是渐进的，而不是突然的。
senses.why: the adjective simply attaches the Latin word for language to any feature of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把拉丁语表「语言」的词挂到语言的任何特征上。

senses.title: Relating to the discipline of linguistics
senses.definition: belonging to the scientific study of language as a field
senses.definitionCN: 属于把语言作为研究对象的科学领域
senses.example: The paper appeared in a linguistic journal, not a literary one.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文发表在一份语言学刊物上，而非文学刊物。
senses.why: the noun for the field and the adjective for it differ by one ending, so the same description covers both language and its study.
senses.whyCN: 学科名词与它的形容词只差一个词尾，因此同一描述既覆盖语言，也覆盖对语言的研究。

senses.title: Inner knowledge of grammar
senses.titleCN: 说话者内在的语法知识
senses.definition: describing the tacit knowledge a speaker has of the rules of a language
senses.definitionCN: 描述说话者对某一语言规则的默会知识
senses.example: Children's linguistic competence grows faster than their vocabulary lists suggest.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童的语言能力增长得比词汇表所显示的更快。
senses.why: the discipline drew a line between what a speaker knows and what a speaker does.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科在「说话者知道什么」与「说话者做什么」之间划了一条线。

senses.title: A minority defined by its tongue
senses.titleCN: 以语言划分的少数群体
senses.definition: naming a community distinguished by the language it speaks
senses.definitionCN: 指以所说语言而区分出来的群体
senses.example: Linguistic minorities won the right to local schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言少数群体争取到了地方办学的权利。
senses.why: a community can be marked out by the tongue it uses, and the adjective follows that marker.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体可以由其所用语言标记出来，形容词便跟着这个标记走。

senses.title: Variety across languages
senses.definition: describing the range of different languages and their features
senses.definitionCN: 描述不同语言及其特征的分布范围
senses.example: The region's linguistic diversity is greater than its biological diversity.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的语言多样性超过它的生物多样性。
senses.why: counting different tongues turns the adjective into a word about range.
senses.whyCN: 把不同语言计数，就让这个形容词变成关于「范围」的词。

senses.title: Classification by structure
senses.definition: used of the comparison and classification of language structures
senses.definitionCN: 用于语言结构的比较与分类
senses.example: Linguistic typology groups languages by how they build sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 语言类型学按造句方式给语言分组。
senses.why: to compare structures is to classify them, and classification is another face of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 比较结构就是给结构分类，而分类是这个形容词的另一副面孔。

senses.title: A barrier caused by language
senses.definition: describing an obstacle that arises because people do not share a tongue
senses.definitionCN: 描述因人们不共用一种语言而产生的障碍
senses.example: The linguistic barrier mattered more than the border itself.
senses.exampleCN: 语言障碍比边界本身更要紧。
senses.why: where tongues differ, communication can fail, so the adjective also names an obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 语言不同处，交流可能失败，因此这个形容词也指障碍。

senses.title: Wording used as evidence
senses.definition: describing features of wording that can identify or date a text
senses.definitionCN: 描述可用于识别或为文本定年的措辞特征
senses.example: Linguistic evidence placed the letter in the late sixteenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 语言证据把这封信定在十六世纪后期。
senses.why: wording leaves traces that can be read, so the adjective moves from language to evidence.
senses.whyCN: 措辞留下可读的痕迹，因此这个形容词从语言转到证据。

intro.en: Linguistic is a nineteenth-century adjective built on Latin lingua 'tongue, language' with the ending -isticus, probably through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是十九世纪形成的形容词，建在拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」之上，带拉丁形容词词尾，很可能经法语传入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue' and 'language'; its deeper origin is unsettled and is not demonstrated by any attested older form.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」；其更深来源无定论，也没有任何可证实的更早形式。

items.en: The ending -isticus, taken from Greek, built adjectives meaning 'of or relating to a practice or field'.
items.cn: 这个源自希腊语的词尾构成形容词，意为「属于或关于某实践或领域的」。

items.en: French formed linguistique for the study of language in the early nineteenth century, and English took the adjective soon after.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪初为语言研究造出相应形容词，英语随后借入。

items.en: As linguistics became a university subject, the adjective came to mean both 'of language' and 'of the discipline'.
items.cn: 随着语言学成为大学学科，这个形容词既指「语言的」，也指「语言学的」。

items.en: The twentieth century added phrases such as linguistic minority and linguistic evidence, extending the adjective into law and history.
items.cn: 二十世纪增加了「语言少数群体」「语言证据」等说法，把这个形容词扩展到法律与历史领域。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the root is unknown, and the exact first English printing of the adjective is not documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：该词根在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个形容词最早的英语印刷记录亦无确切文献。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root words that are easily swapped for the adjective; group two holds adjectives describing language matters.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、容易与这个形容词混用的词；第二组是描述语言事务的形容词。

entries.definition: The name of the discipline; the adjective describes something within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科名称；形容词则描述该学科之内的事物。

entries.definition: A person who studies language; it is a noun for a doer.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，是表施动者的名词。

entries.definition: The system itself; the adjective cannot stand for the system.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统本身；形容词不能替代那个系统。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of the tongue' in anatomy or dentistry, not 'of language'.
entries.definitionCN: 在解剖与牙科中指「舌的」，而非「语言的」。

entries.definition: Relating to words as opposed to actions; it does not refer to grammar or language systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指以词语而非行动表达，不涉及语法或语言系统。

entries.definition: Concerned with meaning rather than structure; it is one part of what linguistic covers.
entries.definitionCN: 关注意义而非结构，是语言研究覆盖的一部分。

entries.definition: Concerned with grammar or with whether a sentence is well formed.
entries.definitionCN: 关注语法或句子是否合式。

entries.definition: Relating to the older study of texts and languages; it is historical where linguistic is general.
entries.definitionCN: 指较旧的文本与语言考据之学，偏历史，而「语言的」更宽泛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The adjective carries the same root as the noun for tongue, so it always points back to speech.
normal.cn: 这个形容词与表「舌头」的名词共享词根，因此总指向言语。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the fields: linguistic diversity, linguistic evidence, linguistic minority.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示领域：语言多样性、语言证据、语言少数群体。

normal.en: The adverb adds a manner: linguistically speaking.
normal.cn: 副词加上方式：从语言上说。

normal.en: The family runs language, linguist, linguistics, bilingual, multilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言」「语言学家」「语言学」「双语的」「多语的」。

normal.en: A text marked with arrows between clauses is the picture to keep.
normal.cn: 在分句之间画箭头的那页文本，是要留住的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a fingerprint made of vowels instead of ridges.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚由元音而非纹路组成的指纹。

abstract.en: Picture a map whose borders follow the spread of words.
abstract.cn: 想象一张边界沿着词语传播而画的图。

abstract.en: Picture a fence built between two villages out of untranslated signs.
abstract.cn: 想象两个村子之间用无法翻译的标牌搭成的一道栅栏。

examples.en: Linguistic differences often survive political union by centuries.
examples.cn: 语言差异常常在政治统一之后还延续几个世纪。

examples.en: The court accepted linguistic analysis as evidence of authorship.
examples.cn: 法庭接受语言分析作为作者身份的证据。

examples.en: Linguistic minorities asked for bilingual ballots.
examples.cn: 语言少数群体要求提供双语选票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林归斯提克」——林子里归拢来的那套说话规矩，就是语言的。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加源自希腊语的形容词词尾构成，十九世纪经法语进入英语，指「语言的」，后也指「语言学的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all attach the adjective to a different object: the language itself, the discipline, the speaker's inner rules, a community, a range of tongues, a classification, a barrier and a piece of evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把这个形容词挂到不同对象上：语言本身、学科、说话者的内在规则、一个群体、语言的范围、一种分类、一道障碍以及一份证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a manuscript page where clauses are linked by thin arrows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页手稿，分句之间用细箭头相连。

branches.en: THE SIMPLEST LINK: any feature of a language can take the adjective.
branches.cn: 最简单的连接：语言的任何特征都能带这个形容词。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the same adjective also marks work done inside the discipline.
branches.cn: 学科：同一个形容词也标记学科内部的研究。

branches.en: INSIDE THE SPEAKER: tacit grammatical knowledge is a linguistic fact too.
branches.cn: 说话者之内：默会的语法知识同样是语言事实。

branches.en: GROUPS AND RANGES: communities are defined by tongues, and tongues differ widely.
branches.cn: 群体与范围：社群由语言界定，而语言彼此差异很大。

branches.en: ORDER, OBSTACLE, PROOF: structure can be classified, difference can block, and wording can testify.
branches.cn: 秩序、障碍与证据：结构可被分类，差异会成阻碍，而措辞可以提供证明。

intro.en: The word is a Latin-rooted adjective with a Greek-derived ending, so it can be read as root plus ending.
intro.cn: 这是一个带拉丁词根与希腊来源词尾的形容词，可按「词根加词尾」来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua supplies the root; the ending came into Latin from Greek and later built many English adjectives of fields and practices.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 提供词根；词尾经拉丁语来自希腊语，后来构成许多英语中表领域与实践的形容词。

items.example: The root ties every sense back to speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把每个义项都系回言语。

items.structure: Greek-derived ending via Latin, 'of or relating to'
items.meaning: belonging to a field or practice
items.example: The ending turns a field into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把领域变成描述词。

items.example: Language is the object the adjective points to.
items.exampleCN: 语言是这个形容词所指的对象。

items.example: A linguist works on sound, grammar or meaning.
items.exampleCN: 语言研究者研究声音、语法或意义。

items.example: Linguistics has its own methods and journals.
items.exampleCN: 语言学有自己的方法与期刊。

items.example: The two regions are linguistically close.
items.exampleCN: 这两个地区在语言上很接近。

items.example: Bilingual education began in the border counties.
items.exampleCN: 双语教育从边境各县开始。

items.example: A multilingual staff serves the port.
items.exampleCN: 一支多语员工队伍服务这个港口。

definition_zh: 语言学（研究语言的结构、使用与历史的学科）
definition_en: the scientific study of language, including its sounds, structure, meaning, use and history
core_image: 一张铺开的长桌上摆着录音机、音标卡片与写着句法树的黑板照片，四角用镇纸压住
scene: 研究室的桌上摆着录音机、音标卡片与一张句法树的照片，四角都用镇纸压住。Modern linguistics borrows methods from psychology and computer science.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究语言结构、使用与历史的学科」（第 1 个义项：把语言作为科学研究对象的学问）；句意为现代语言学从心理学与计算机科学借用方法。可辨识物件：录音机、音标卡片、句法树、镇纸。

pos.zh: 语言学（作单数；指分支或学派时可用复数）

senses.title: The science of language in general
senses.definition: the systematic study of how languages are structured, learned and used
senses.definitionCN: 对语言如何构成、习得与使用的系统研究
senses.example: Linguistics asks how children acquire grammar without being taught it.
senses.exampleCN: 语言学追问儿童如何在无人教授的情况下习得语法。
senses.why: the name was formed from the adjective for language plus a suffix naming a field of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个名称由表「语言的」形容词加表研究领域的后缀构成。

senses.title: A particular school of theory
senses.definition: one theoretical framework within the field, such as structural or generative linguistics
senses.definitionCN: 该领域内的某一理论框架，如结构主义或生成语法语言学
senses.example: Generative linguistics dominated the department for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 生成语法语言学在这个系主导了三十年。
senses.why: a shared framework gives the field a recognisable shape, and each framework takes the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 共享框架给学科一个可辨认的形状，每一个框架都沿用学科之名。

senses.title: A subfield or department
senses.definition: a named branch or organizational unit, such as applied linguistics
senses.definitionCN: 具名的分支或有组织的单位，如应用语言学
senses.example: Applied linguistics sits between teaching and research.
senses.exampleCN: 应用语言学处在教学与研究之间。
senses.why: universities divide the field into named units, and each unit carries the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 大学把学科分成具名单位，每个单位都带着学科之名。

senses.title: The historical study of languages
senses.definition: the branch that traces how sounds, words and forms change over time
senses.definitionCN: 追踪语音、词汇与形式随时间变化的那个分支
senses.example: Historical linguistics can date a split between two dialects.
senses.exampleCN: 历史语言学能为两种方言的分化定年。
senses.why: change over time is one of the field's oldest questions, so the branch keeps the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 随时间变化是这门学科最古老的问题之一，因此该分支保留学科之名。

senses.title: Language in its social setting
senses.titleCN: 社会情境中的语言研究
senses.definition: the branch that studies how class, gender and region shape speech
senses.definitionCN: 研究阶层、性别与地区如何塑造言语的分支
senses.example: Sociolinguistics showed that the same speaker shifts style by audience.
senses.exampleCN: 社会语言学表明，同一个说话者会随听众改变语体。
senses.why: speech varies with company, and that variation is studied under the field's name.
senses.whyCN: 言语随交往对象而变，这种变异也在学科名下被研究。

senses.title: Language handled by machines
senses.titleCN: 由机器处理的语言研究
senses.definition: the branch that builds models and tools for automatic language processing
senses.definitionCN: 建立自动语言处理模型与工具的分支
senses.example: Computational linguistics made the translation tool possible.
senses.exampleCN: 计算语言学使这款翻译工具成为可能。
senses.why: machines need formal models of language, which the field supplies.
senses.whyCN: 机器需要语言的形式模型，而这正是该学科提供的。

senses.title: Linguistic analysis as a method
senses.definition: the use of linguistic techniques to analyse a text, a dispute or a recording
senses.definitionCN: 用语言技术分析文本、争议或录音
senses.example: The lawsuit turned on linguistics as much as on law.
senses.exampleCN: 这起诉讼的胜负，语言学与法律同样关键。
senses.why: the discipline's name is borrowed whenever its methods are applied outside it.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的方法一旦被用到别处，学科名也随之被借用。

senses.title: The descriptive study of one language
senses.titleCN: 对单一语言的描写研究
senses.definition: the detailed description of a single language's sound system and grammar
senses.definitionCN: 对某一种语言语音系统与语法的细致描写
senses.example: The linguistics of the island's sign language is still barely recorded.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛屿手语的语言学研究几乎还没有记录。
senses.why: the field can also be narrowed to a single tongue, and the name stays.
senses.whyCN: 学科也可以收窄到单一语言，名称保持不变。

intro.en: Linguistics is the adjective linguistic plus the field-naming ending -s, modelled on French and German terms of the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是在形容词「语言的」上加表研究领域的词尾构成，仿照十九世纪的法语与德语说法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant 'tongue, language'. Its deeper origin is unsettled, and no older form is attested.
items.cn: lingua 意为「舌头、语言」，其更深来源无定论，也没有更早形式的书证。

items.en: French used a single term for the study of language in the early nineteenth century, and English took both the adjective and the field name from it.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪初用一个词指语言研究，英语从它借入了形容词与学科名。

items.en: German scholarship also fixed a name for the new science, which helped the English noun settle.
items.cn: 德语学界也为这门新科学定下名称，促成了英语名词的定型。

items.en: English formed the noun in the nineteenth century and made it singular in use, even though it ends like a plural.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪构成这个名词，尽管词尾形似复数，实际作单数使用。

items.en: The twentieth century multiplied named branches, from sociolinguistics to computational linguistics.
items.cn: 二十世纪不断衍生具名分支，从社会语言学一直到计算语言学。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first fixed use of the English field name is not precisely dated, and the pre-Latin root remains unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个英语学科名最早的确切使用年代不明，其在拉丁语之前的词根亦未知。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root forms that are always being confused; group two holds neighbouring fields.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而总被混淆的词形；第二组是相邻的学科。

entries.definition: Describes something as relating to language; it is not the name of the field.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物与语言有关，并非学科名称。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the field, or loosely a speaker of many languages.
entries.definitionCN: 指该领域的从业者，或宽泛地指会说多种语言的人。

entries.definition: The thing the field studies; the discipline and its object are different words.
entries.definitionCN: 指被研究的对象；学科与其对象是两个不同的词。

entries.definition: The historical study of texts and languages; linguistics grew partly out of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指对文本与语言的历史考据，语言学有一部分由它发展而来。

entries.definition: The branch studying speech sounds; it is one part of linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 研究语音的分支，是语言学的一部分。

entries.definition: The study of how words combine into sentences, a core branch of the field.
entries.definitionCN: 研究词如何组合成句，是该领域的核心分支。

entries.definition: The study of meaning in language, another branch of linguistics.
entries.definitionCN: 研究语言中的意义，是语言学的另一分支。

entries.definition: The rules themselves or a book of them; linguistics studies grammar rather than prescribing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则本身或规则书；语言学研究语法而不规定语法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The name looks plural but works as a singular, like many names of sciences.
normal.cn: 这个名称形似复数，却作单数用，许多学科名都是如此。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the branches: applied, historical and computational linguistics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配列出分支：应用语言学、历史语言学、计算语言学。

normal.en: The adjective, the person and the field differ only by their endings.
normal.cn: 形容词、人与学科只差各自的词尾。

normal.en: The family runs linguist, linguistic, sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言学家」「语言的」「社会语言学」「心理语言学」。

normal.en: A desk with a recorder and a syntax tree is the picture of the discipline at work.
normal.cn: 摆着录音机与句法树的桌子，就是这门学科工作时的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a grammar treated like a living organism under a lens.
abstract.cn: 想象把语法当作镜头下的活体来观察。

abstract.en: Picture a map of sounds rather than of roads.
abstract.cn: 想象一张声音的地图，而不是道路的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where sentences are taken apart and rebuilt.
abstract.cn: 想象一间工坊，句子被拆开又重新装回。

examples.en: Linguistics turned the study of grammar from prescription into description.
examples.cn: 语言学把语法研究从规定转向描写。

examples.en: She took linguistics because she wanted to understand her own dialect.
examples.cn: 她学语言学，是因为想弄懂自己的方言。

examples.en: Computational linguistics now fills the translation apps people use daily.
examples.cn: 计算语言学如今支撑着人们日常使用的翻译应用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「林归斯提克斯」——把林子里的说话方式全部归拢、分类、拆开看，就是语言学。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」加希腊来源的形容词词尾，再叠加表研究领域的词尾构成；十九世纪仿法语与德语说法定型，指研究语言的科学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name the same science but from different angles: the whole field, a theory, a department, history, society, machines, a borrowed method, and the description of a single tongue.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指同一门科学，只是角度不同：整个领域、一种理论、一个院系、历史、社会、机器、被借用的方法，以及对单一语言的描写。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recorder, phonetic cards and a syntax tree pinned under paperweights.
core.cn: 核心意象：录音机、音标卡片与被镇纸压住的句法树。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the general science of language is the trunk of every other use.
branches.cn: 整体：研究语言的一般科学是其他用法的树干。

branches.en: ORGANIZED FORMS: a theory and a department are the field given a shape.
branches.cn: 有形的组织：理论，院系，是这门领域获得形状的方式。

branches.en: TIME AND COMPANY: languages change across centuries and shift with audience.
branches.cn: 时间与同伴：语言跨越世纪而变，也随听众而变。

branches.en: FROM MACHINES TO ONE TONGUE: the field ranges from automatic processing to a single sign language.
branches.cn: 从机器到单一语言：这门学问既研究自动处理，也描写一种手语。

branches.en: BORROWED METHODS: once the techniques travel, the field's name travels with them.
branches.cn: 被借用的方法：技术一旦外流，学科名也随之而去。

intro.en: The word is an adjective plus a field-naming ending, and its root also builds the family of language words.
intro.cn: 这个词是形容词加表领域的词尾构成，其词根也构成「语言」一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua supplies the root; the Greek-derived ending for fields passed through Latin and French before English fixed the name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 提供词根；表领域的希腊来源词尾经拉丁语与法语，最终在英语中定名。

items.example: The root names both the organ and its product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼指器官与其产物。

items.structure: Greek-derived ending for fields of study
items.example: The ending builds names such as physics and ethics.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成「物理学」「伦理学」等名称。

items.example: The linguist analysed the vowel system.
items.exampleCN: 这位语言学家分析了元音系统。

items.meaning: of language or of the field
items.example: Linguistic data filled three notebooks.

definition_zh: 链环；连接物；纽带；连接；关联；链接
definition_en: one ring of a chain; something that joins two things; to connect or associate people, objects, or ideas
core_image: 两段铁链由中间一个环扣住，环环相扣，力量沿链条传递
scene: 铁路调度室里，调度员把两个货运站接进同一条新支线。He used the panel to link the two freight yards to the new branch line, and a green line appeared between the two dots.
sceneCN: 这里 link 是「把两点连成一条线路」（第 6 个义项：交通连线）；句意：他用调度台把两个货运站连到新支线上，屏幕上两点之间多出一条绿线。图中可辨识物件：铁路线路图、两个货运站标记、新支线绿线、调度台；对应第 1 个义项。

连接；联系；把……串起来

collocations.zh: A 与 B 之间的联系

senses.title: Chain ring: one loop in a chain
senses.definition: a single ring of metal that forms one unit of a chain
senses.definitionCN: 构成链条一个单元的单个金属环
senses.example: One link of the chain had rusted through.
senses.exampleCN: 链条上有一个环已经锈穿了。
senses.why: The earliest English sense is the physical ring. Everything else grows from this object: a chain is a row of rings, and each ring holds the next.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的义项就是这种实体环。其余义项都从这一物件生长出来：链条是一排环，而每个环都扣住下一个。

senses.title: Connector: a piece that joins two ends
senses.titleCN: 连接件：把两端扣在一起的部件
senses.definition: a physical part or device that fastens two separate parts together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个分离部件扣合在一起的实体部件或装置
senses.example: A steel link joined the two sections of the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 一个钢制连接件把围栏的两段接了起来。
senses.why: A chain ring already does the work of holding two neighbours. The word is therefore ready to name any small piece whose job is to join two ends.
senses.whyCN: 链环本来就在承担“扣住左右两环”的工作。因此这个词很自然地可以指任何以“接合两端”为职责的小部件。

senses.title: Bond between people or groups
senses.titleCN: 纽带：人与人、群体与群体之间的联结
senses.definition: a relationship or connection between people, groups, or organizations
senses.definitionCN: 人与人、群体或组织之间的关系或联结
senses.example: The exchange programme created a lasting link between the two schools.
senses.exampleCN: 交换项目在两所学校之间建立了持久的纽带。
senses.why: Move from metal to society: the ring that held two chain ends now holds two people or institutions. The connection is no longer visible, but it still constrains and carries.
senses.whyCN: 从金属转向社会：原本扣住两节链子的环，现在扣住两个人或两个机构。联结不再可见，但仍在约束与传递。

senses.title: Join physically: connect two things
senses.titleCN: 实体连接：把两件东西接起来
senses.definition: to connect two objects or places so that they are joined or can work together
senses.definitionCN: 把两个物体或地点连接起来，使其接合或能协同运作
senses.example: Workers linked the new pipe to the old water main.
senses.exampleCN: 工人把新管道接到旧的总水管上。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: to link is to act as the ring, putting oneself or a part between two ends and holding them together.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：link 就是充当那个环，把自己或某个部件放在两端之间，把它们扣住。

senses.title: Associate ideas or evidence
senses.titleCN: 关联：把观念、证据或因果串起来
senses.definition: to show or establish a connection between ideas, facts, or causes
senses.definitionCN: 表明或建立观念、事实或原因之间的联系
senses.example: The study links long commutes to higher stress levels.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把长途通勤与更高的压力水平联系起来。
senses.why: A chain of reasoning is also a row of rings: each claim holds the next. To link two facts is to insert the ring that makes them one sequence rather than two isolated items.
senses.whyCN: 推理链同样是一排环：每个论断扣住下一个。把两个事实 link 起来，就是插入那个让它们成为一条序列、而非两个孤立项的环。

senses.title: Transport connection: a route between two points
senses.titleCN: 交通连线：连接两点的线路
senses.definition: a transport route or service that connects two places
senses.definitionCN: 连接两地的交通路线或运输服务
senses.example: The new rail link cuts the journey to forty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 新的铁路连线把行程缩短到四十分钟。
senses.why: Two stations are like two chain ends; the rail line is the ring that joins them into one network. The image scales from a hand-held chain to a map.
senses.whyCN: 两个车站就像链条的两端，铁路线则是把二者接入同一网络的环。这个意象从手中的链条放大到地图上。

senses.title: Digital link: hyperlink or network connection
senses.titleCN: 数字链接：超链接或网络连接
senses.definition: a hyperlink in a document, or a connection between computers or network nodes
senses.definitionCN: 文档中的超链接，或计算机、网络节点之间的连接
senses.example: Click the link to open the full report.
senses.exampleCN: 点击链接打开完整报告。
senses.why: A webpage is a node and a hyperlink is the ring that carries a reader from one page to another. The same join-and-carry structure is now made of protocol rather than metal.
senses.whyCN: 网页是一个节点，超链接则是把读者从一页带到另一页的环。同样的“接合与传递”结构，如今由协议而不是金属构成。

senses.title: Link arms: join bodies in contact
senses.definition: to join arms or hands with someone, especially as a sign of closeness or support
senses.definitionCN: 与某人挽臂或牵手，尤表示亲近或相互支持
senses.example: The two friends linked arms and walked into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 两个朋友挽着手臂走进大厅。
senses.why: Here the human body supplies both ends: bent arms form the rings. The verb returns to its most concrete physical action while keeping the idea of mutual holding.
senses.whyCN: 这里两端都由人体提供：弯起的手臂就是环。动词回到最具体的身体动作，同时保留“相互扣住”的意思。

senses.title: Missing link: the absent ring in a sequence
senses.titleCN: 缺环：序列中缺失的一环
senses.definition: in the phrase missing link, the absent piece needed to complete an evolutionary or logical chain
senses.definitionCN: 用于 missing link，指完成演化链或论证链所缺的那一环
senses.example: The fossil was hailed as the missing link between the two species.
senses.exampleCN: 这块化石被誉为两个物种之间缺失的一环。
senses.why: If a chain is only as strong as its rings, one absent ring breaks the sequence. The phrase turns a physical gap into a metaphor for an unexplained step.
senses.whyCN: 如果链条的强度取决于每一环，那么缺一个环就断了整条序列。这个短语把实体缺口变成了“无法解释的中间步骤”的隐喻。

senses.title: Link up: separate parts meet and join
senses.titleCN: 汇合：分开的部分相遇并联结
senses.definition: in the phrasal verb link up, to join or meet after being separate
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语动词 link up，表示原本分开的部分连接或会合
senses.example: The two rescue teams linked up at the tunnel entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 两支救援队在隧道口会合了。
senses.why: The particle up adds completion: the ring is not merely placed but closed. Separate parties become one continuous chain, which is why the phrase suits meetings and mergers.
senses.whyCN: 小品词 up 补充“完成”：环不只是放上去，而是扣合封闭。分开的各方变成一条连续的链，因此这个短语适合会合与合并。

intro.en: Link was borrowed from Old Norse, not inherited from Old English. The chain-ring sense is solid; the jump to a bend root in Indo-European is generally believed rather than proved.
intro.cn: link 是从古诺斯语借入的，而不是从古英语继承的。链环义很确定；上溯到印欧语“弯曲”词根则属于一般认为是，而非已经证明。

items.en: The noun probably comes from Old Norse hlekkr 'link of a chain', with a related verb hlekkja 'to chain'. Old Norse gave English many everyday words during the Viking period.
items.cn: 名词很可能来自古诺斯语 hlekkr“链环”，并有相关动词 hlekkja“用链子拴住”。维京时期古诺斯语给英语带来了大量日常词。

items.en: The Norse word is traced to Proto-Germanic *hlankiz, a formation from a root meaning 'to bend'. A ring is metal bent back on itself.
items.cn: 这个诺斯语词可追溯到原始日耳曼语 *hlankiz，由表示“弯曲”的词根构成。环就是金属弯回自身形成的形状。

items.en: The deeper source is generally believed to be PIE *kleng- 'to bend, turn'. The same family is often linked to angle and other bend words, but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 更深的来源一般认为是原始印欧语 *kleng-“弯曲、转折”。同一词族常被与 angle 等“弯折”词联系起来，但这一重构并不确定。

items.en: English records the noun in the early 15c. and the verb in the late 14c., first in the literal sense of fitting with chain links.
items.cn: 英语中名词最早记录于 15 世纪早期，动词记录于 14 世纪晚期，最初都是“装上链环”的字面义。

items.en: From a metal ring the word extends to any connection: rail links, personal links, links between facts, and finally hyperlinks. The chain image survives in missing link and weakest link.
items.cn: 从金属环出发，这个词扩展到任何连接：铁路连线、人际纽带、事实之间的关联，最后是超链接。链条意象仍活在 missing link 与 weakest link 中。

note.en: The first group tests spelling and derivation around link; the second separates four kinds of connection by strength, direction, and domain.
note.cn: 第一组检查 link 周围的拼写与派生关系；第二组按强度、方向和领域区分四种“连接”。

entries.definition: the act or system of linking; a mechanical or genetic connection. It is link plus the noun suffix -age.
entries.definitionCN: 连接行为或连接系统；机械或遗传上的联动。它是 link 加名词后缀 -age。

entries.definition: to shut and open the eyes quickly. It rhymes and looks close but has a different, uncertain origin.
entries.definitionCN: 快速眨眼。它押韵、词形接近，但来源不同且不确定。

entries.definition: coloured liquid used for writing or printing. It shares the -ink ending only; there is no link in it.
entries.definitionCN: 用于书写或印刷的彩色液体。它只共享 -ink 结尾，与 link 没有词源关系。

entries.definition: to join two things so that they touch or work together. It is the broad neutral verb, while link often suggests a chain-like intermediate part.
entries.definitionCN: 把两物接合，使其接触或协同运作。它是最宽泛中性的动词，而 link 常暗示有一个链环式的中间部件。

entries.definition: to fasten one thing to another, usually a smaller thing to a larger one. It stresses physical fixing, not mutual relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 把一物固定到另一物上，通常是小物附于大物。它强调实体固定，而不是相互关联。

entries.definition: to tie or fasten tightly, or to place under a moral or legal obligation. It is stronger and more restrictive than link.
entries.definitionCN: 紧紧捆扎或固定，或使承担道德、法律义务。它比 link 更强、更具约束力。

entries.definition: the way two people or groups are connected and behave toward each other. It names the durable social tie that link describes.
entries.definitionCN: 两个人或群体相互连接与相处的方式。它命名了 link 所描述的那种持久社会纽带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the physical chain ring, the fixed phrases missing link and weakest link, and the modern hyperlink.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：实体的链环、固定短语 missing link 与 weakest link，以及现代的超链接。

normal.en: A chain is a row of rings; one ring is a link. Take one out and the chain falls apart.
normal.cn: 链条是一排环，一个环就是一个 link。取走一个，整条链就散了。

normal.en: The weakest link is the ring that breaks first, so the phrase means the most vulnerable part of any system.
normal.cn: weakest link 是最先断的那个环，因此这个短语指任何系统中最脆弱的部分。

normal.en: The missing link is the ring absent from a sequence, especially an evolutionary chain.
normal.cn: missing link 是序列中缺失的那个环，尤指演化链上的缺环。

normal.en: Link up means the ring is finally closed: two separate parties meet and become one chain.
normal.cn: link up 表示环终于扣合：两个分开的方会合，变成一条链。

normal.en: A hyperlink does the same job on the web: one click carries you from one page to the next.
normal.cn: 超链接在网络上做同一件事：一次点击把你从一页带到下一页。

abstract.en: Two islands with a bridge between them: the bridge is not either island, yet without it they are separate worlds.
abstract.cn: 两座岛之间有一座桥：桥不属于任何一座岛，但没有它，两座岛就是分开的世界。

abstract.en: A chain has no centre: every ring holds the next and is held by the previous, so the link is a position rather than a thing.
abstract.cn: 链条没有中心：每个环都扣住下一个，又被上一个扣住，因此“环”是一种位置，而不是一个孤立物件。

abstract.en: A web of nodes and edges: the nodes are what we see, the links are the invisible lines along which influence travels.
abstract.cn: 由节点和边构成的网：节点是我们看得见的东西，链接则是影响沿之传递的看不见的线。

examples.en: The bridge links the island to the mainland.
examples.cn: 这座桥把海岛与大陆连接起来。

examples.en: Researchers have found a link between sleep loss and poor memory.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠不足与记忆力差之间存在关联。

examples.en: Send me the link to the recording when it is ready.
examples.cn: 录音准备好后把链接发给我。

dict_mnemonic.text: “林克”——游戏主角林克把地图上的各个地点串起来 → link 连接

root: 古诺斯语 hlekkr“链环”，原始日耳曼语 *hlankiz；核心是“一环扣一环”，引申为任何连接、纽带与关联。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of link, all built on one object: a ring that holds two ends together. The ring becomes a connector, a human bond, a route, a hyperlink, a missing step, and finally the act of closing the chain.
sensesIntro.cn: link 的十个义项都建立在一个物件上：把两端扣住的环。这个环变成连接件、人际纽带、线路、超链接、缺失的步骤，最后变成“把链扣合”的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ring holds the ring before it and the ring after it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个环同时扣住前一个环与后一个环。

branches.en: PHYSICAL RING: the literal chain link and any part that fastens two ends.
branches.cn: 实体环：字面的链环，以及任何接合两端的部件。

branches.en: HUMAN CONTACT: the ring becomes a bond between people or a joining of arms.
branches.cn: 人际接触：环变成人与人之间的纽带，或手臂的相互扣住。

branches.en: INFRASTRUCTURE: pipes, rails and routes are rings that join places into a network.
branches.cn: 基础设施：管道、铁路与航线都是把地点接入网络的环。

branches.en: LOGICAL CHAIN: facts are linked like rings, and a missing ring explains why a sequence fails.
branches.cn: 逻辑链：事实像环一样被串起，缺环则解释了序列为何断裂。

branches.en: DIGITAL AND COMPLETION: a hyperlink carries a reader, and link up closes the ring.
branches.cn: 数字与完成：超链接把读者带过去，link up 则把环扣合封闭。

intro.en: Link is a borrowed Germanic noun and verb, not a prefixed Latin word. English adds -age, -ed, -er and -ing to build its family.
intro.cn: link 是借入的日耳曼语名词兼动词，不是带前缀的拉丁词。英语通过 -age、-ed、-er、-ing 构成它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Link has no Latin ancestor. If the Indo-European bend root *kleng- is correct, it is a distant cousin of angle, ankle and anchor, but that link is generally believed rather than established.
latinIntro.cn: link 没有拉丁语祖先。如果印欧语“弯曲”词根 *kleng- 成立，它与 angle、ankle、anchor 是远亲，但这一联系只是一般认为，并未确立。

items.meaning: the act or system of linking; a mechanical or genetic connection
items.meaningCN: 连接；联系；联动机制（-age 构成行为或系统名词）
items.example: The linkage between the two levers controls the brake.
items.exampleCN: 两根杠杆之间的联动机构控制刹车。

items.meaningCN: 相连的；有关联的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The two problems are closely linked.

items.meaning: a program or device that joins separate pieces
items.meaningCN: 连接程序；链接器（-er 表示执行该动作的物）
items.example: The linker combines the object files into one program.
items.exampleCN: 链接器把多个目标文件合并成一个程序。

items.meaning: the act of connecting; serving to connect
items.meaningCN: 连接；起连接作用的（-ing 构成动作或功能词）
items.example: A linking verb joins a subject to its description.
items.exampleCN: 连系动词把主语与其描述连接起来。

items.example: It forms linkage, a set of connections.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 linkage，即一组连接。

items.example: You can unlink the file from the message.
items.exampleCN: 你可以把文件从消息里解除链接。

items.example: The two networks are interlinked.

items.meaning: a clickable cross-reference on a page
items.example: Click the hyperlink to open the source.

items.meaning: a joining of two systems or groups
items.example: The rail link-up took ten years to complete.
items.exampleCN: 这条铁路的接轨花了十年才完成。

latinEntries.meaning: a corner or the space between two lines
latinEntries.meaningCN: 角；两条线之间的空间（与“弯曲”词根有远亲关系）

latinEntries.structure: Old English ancleow, from PIE *ang- (to bend)
latinEntries.meaning: the joint where the foot bends
a heavy device that holds a ship in place
latinEntries.meaningCN: 锚；把船固定住的重物（原义与“弯钩”有关）
三角形；有三个角的平面图形

definition_zh: 液体的；液态的；流动而清澈的；（资产）易变现的；现金充裕的
definition_en: in the state of a substance that flows freely, clear and smooth, or easily converted into cash

液体；液态物

senses.title: A substance that flows freely
senses.titleCN: 能自由流动的物质状态
senses.definition: matter with a definite volume but no fixed shape, which takes the shape of its container
senses.definitionCN: 有一定体积而无固定形状、随容器改变形状的物质
senses.example: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 汞是室温下唯一呈液态的金属。
senses.why: the adjective describes the state itself, and the noun names any substance in it, so the pair covers water, oil and melted metal.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述这一状态本身，名词指处于该状态的任何物质，因此水、油与熔化的金属都包括在内。

senses.title: Clear and translucent, as light or eyes
senses.titleCN: 清澈透亮的，如光或眼睛
senses.definition: describing something that lets light through and looks deep rather than cloudy
senses.definitionCN: 描述透光、显得深澈而不浑浊之物
senses.example: The lake was liquid green in the early sun.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨阳光下，湖面泛着清澈的绿。
senses.why: clear water was the original sight behind the word, and the quality was transferred to anything that seems to hold light within.
senses.whyCN: 清水是这个词背后的原始景象，这一性质随后被移到任何仿佛内含光亮之物上。

senses.title: Smooth and flowing in movement or sound
senses.titleCN: 动作或声音的流畅圆润
senses.definition: describing motion or music that runs without jerks, like a stream
senses.definitionCN: 描述动作或音乐毫无顿挫、如水般流淌
senses.example: Her liquid phrasing made the sonata seem easy.
senses.exampleCN: 她流畅的乐句让这首奏鸣曲显得轻松。
senses.why: what flows without obstruction is pleasant to watch or hear, so the physical idea became a word of praise for grace.
senses.whyCN: 无阻流动之物看着听着都舒服，物理观念于是变成赞美优雅的词。

senses.title: Easily turned into cash
senses.definition: describing an asset that can be sold quickly without a loss
senses.definitionCN: 描述能迅速售出而不损失价值的资产
senses.example: Treasury bills are the most liquid asset in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 短期国库券是市场上最容易变现的资产。
senses.why: cash itself flows, so an asset that becomes cash at once is described with the same word as water.
senses.whyCN: 现金本身会流动，能立刻变成现金的资产便与水共用同一个词。

senses.title: A market with many ready buyers
senses.definition: describing a market where large orders are absorbed without moving the price much
senses.definitionCN: 描述能吸收大额订单而价格变动不大的市场
senses.example: The shares became liquid only after the index inclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这些股票被纳入指数之后才变得易于成交。
senses.why: a market is liquid when orders wait on both sides, so a seller meets a buyer instead of waiting.
senses.whyCN: 市场两侧都挂着订单时才算易成交，卖方能直接遇到买方而不必等待。

senses.title: Cash and near-cash funds
senses.definition: describing money held in cash or in instruments that can be spent almost at once
senses.definitionCN: 描述以现金或几乎可即刻支用的票据持有的钱
senses.example: The firm kept half its wealth in liquid form.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业把一半财富以现金形式持有。
senses.why: wealth kept as cash can be spent without selling anything, which is the financial form of the same flow.
senses.whyCN: 以现金持有的财富无需出售任何东西就能支用，这是同一流动在金融上的形态。

senses.title: A liquid consonant in phonetics
senses.definition: describing the sounds l and r, which flow into neighbouring sounds without friction
senses.definitionCN: 描述边音与颤音这类与相邻音平滑相接、不产生摩擦的音
senses.example: English has two liquid consonants in most analyses.
senses.exampleCN: 多数分析认为英语有两个流音。
senses.why: phonetics borrowed the flowing image because these sounds pass into their neighbours without a stop, unlike plosives.
senses.whyCN: 语音学借用「流动」意象，因为这些音与邻音相接而不阻塞，与爆破音不同。

senses.title: A liquid diet in medicine
senses.definition: describing food taken as fluids for a period, often after surgery or during illness
senses.definitionCN: 描述在术后或病中一段时间内以流体形式进食
senses.example: He was on a liquid diet for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃了三天流食。
senses.why: the medical use narrows the adjective to what can be swallowed as fluid, which is the oldest physical sense applied to care.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把这个形容词收窄到可以以流质吞下的食物，这是最古老的物理义被用在照护上。

senses.title: Fluid, unsettled conditions in society
senses.titleCN: 社会中流动不定的状态
senses.definition: describing social or economic arrangements that change constantly and have no fixed form
senses.definitionCN: 描述不断变化、没有固定形态的社会或经济安排
senses.example: Bauman described modern life as liquid because nothing keeps its shape for long.
senses.exampleCN: 鲍曼把现代生活称作液态的，因为没有东西能长久保持形状。
senses.why: the metaphor extends flow from matter to institutions: what is liquid cannot be grasped and held, only followed.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻把流动从物质扩展到制度：液态之物抓不住、握不牢，只能跟随。

intro.en: Liquid comes from Latin liquidus 'fluid, clear', from liquere 'to be fluid'. English took it in the fourteenth century as both adjective and noun. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: liquid 来自拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」，其动词为 liquere「呈液态」。英语于 14 世纪把它同时吸收为形容词与名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Liquere meant 'to be fluid, to flow, to be clear'. Its earlier origin is uncertain, and the common reconstruction is a hypothesis rather than a proved form.
items.cn: liquere 意为「呈液态、流动、清澈」。其更早来源不确定，常见重构只是假说，并非已证形式。

items.en: Liquidus described water, oil and melted substances, and also clear light and a smooth style of speech.
items.cn: liquidus 描述水、油与熔化物，也用于清澈的光与平顺的言辞。

items.en: English liquid appears in the fourteenth century, at first for flowing matter; the noun and the adjective developed together.
items.cn: 英语 liquid 于 14 世纪出现，最初指流动的物质；名词与形容词同时发展。

items.en: Seventeenth-century grammars used liquid for sounds that flow into their neighbours, a technical borrowing of the water image.
items.cn: 17 世纪的语法学用 liquid 指流进邻音的音，这是对水的意象的技术性借用。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the adjective was applied to assets that turn into cash quickly, and liquid assets became a standard phrase.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个形容词被用于能迅速变成现金的资产，「流动资产」成为标准说法。

items.en: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries extended it to social arrangements that will not hold their shape, as in liquid modernity.
items.cn: 20 与 21 世纪把它扩展到无法保持形状的社会安排，如「液态现代性」。

note.en: Group one holds words from the flowing root or close in shape; group two holds adjectives that describe fluids, clarity or easy sale.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「流动」词根或形近的词；第二组是描述流体、清澈或易售的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The ease of turning assets into cash; liquid is the adjective that carries the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指资产变现的容易程度；liquid 是承载同一观念的形容词。

entries.definition: A distilled alcoholic drink, from Latin liquor 'fluid'; the modern sense is a narrow survival.
entries.definitionCN: 指蒸馏酒，来自拉丁 liquor「流体」；现代义是狭窄的存留。

entries.definition: To sell off assets or wind up a firm; it names the action that makes a holding liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 指出售资产或结束企业；它指使持有物变现的动作。

entries.definition: To make something fluid; it is about physical state, not money.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物液化；关乎物理状态，而非金钱。

entries.definition: A substance that flows; it is the everyday term, while liquid is the technical state between solid and gas.
entries.definitionCN: 指流动的物质；它是日常说法，liquid 是固气之间的技术状态。

entries.definition: Easy to see through; it covers the translucent sense but says nothing about flow or cash.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易看透；只覆盖清澈义，与流动或现金无关。

entries.definition: Free from bumps; it covers the flowing-motion sense but not the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有凹凸；覆盖流畅义，但不指物质状态。

entries.definition: Able to find a buyer; liquid adds that the sale is fast and does not move the price.
entries.definitionCN: 指能寻得买家；liquid 另含「卖得快且不压价」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Water is the original picture: it flows, it is clear, and it takes the shape of whatever holds it.
normal.cn: 水是原始图景：会流、清澈，并随容器改变形状。

normal.en: The family runs liquid, liquidity, liquefy, liquefaction, liquidate, liquor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括液体的、流动性、液化、液化过程、清算、蒸馏酒。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: liquid assets, liquid nitrogen, liquid crystal, liquid diet.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：流动资产、液氮、液晶、流食。

normal.en: In finance the test is simple: can it become cash this week without a discount?
normal.cn: 金融上的检验很简单：它这周能不能不折价地变成现金？

normal.en: In phonetics the same word names sounds that glide into their neighbours.
normal.cn: 在语音学中，同一个词指滑入邻音的那些音。

abstract.en: Picture water sliding down the inside of a glass while a coin at the bottom stays visible.
abstract.cn: 想象水沿杯壁滑下，杯底的硬币仍清晰可见。

abstract.en: Picture a stream that takes the shape of every stone it passes.
abstract.cn: 想象一条溪流，随经过的每块石头改变形状。

abstract.en: Picture a city where the buildings are replaced before anyone learns their names.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，楼房在人们记住名字之前就被替换。

examples.en: The doctor put him on a liquid diet for two days after the operation.
examples.cn: 手术后医生让他吃了两天流食。

examples.en: Investors moved into liquid assets as the outlook darkened.
examples.cn: 前景转暗时，投资者转向流动资产。

examples.en: The market is liquid enough for a large order to be filled in minutes.
examples.cn: 这个市场的流动性足以让大额订单在几分钟内成交。

dict_mnemonic.text: 这个词听起来像「流克的」——能流的、清亮的；钱能立刻流成现金，就是易变现的

root: 拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」来自 liquere「呈液态」，更深来源不确定；英语 14 世纪吸收为形容词与名词，17 世纪进入语音学，19 世纪进入金融。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow flow: a substance that flows, light that passes through it, motion that runs smoothly, an asset that becomes cash, a market that absorbs orders, funds kept in cash, a consonant that glides, a diet taken as fluid, and a society that will not hold its shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿「流动」展开：会流的物质、透过它的光、平滑的运行、变成现金的资产、能吸收订单的市场、以现金持有的资金、滑入邻音的音、以流质进食的饮食，以及无法保持形状的社会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water sliding down a glass, clear enough to show the coin beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：水沿玻璃杯滑下，清澈得能看见杯底的硬币。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE AND ITS CLARITY: what flows also lets light through, and both belong to water.
branches.cn: 物质与清澈：会流之物也让光透过，二者都属于水。

branches.en: SMOOTH PASSAGE: motion and consonants alike glide into what follows without a stop.
branches.cn: 平滑过渡：动作与辅音都不阻塞地滑入后接之物。

branches.en: MONEY THAT FLOWS: an asset becomes cash, and the firm keeps its wealth in that form.
branches.cn: 会流的钱：资产变成现金，企业以该形式持有财富。

branches.en: THE MARKET'S DEPTH: many ready buyers let a large order pass without moving the price.
branches.cn: 市场的深度：众多现成买家让大额订单通过而不推动价格。

branches.en: CARE AND METAPHOR: a diet taken as fluid, and a society whose arrangements will not hold their shape.
branches.cn: 照护与隐喻：以流质进食的饮食，以及安排无法定形的社会。

intro.en: Liquid is a Latin adjective for flowing or clear; the same root supplies the noun for liquidity, the verb for melting and the drink called liquor.
intro.cn: liquid 是表示「流动、清澈」的拉丁形容词；同一词根给出表示流动性的名词、表示熔化的动词，以及名为 liquor 的酒。

latinIntro.en: Latin liquere and liquidus stand behind this whole family, from liquid and liquidity to liquefy and liquor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 liquere 与 liquidus 支撑整个词族，从 liquid、liquidity 到 liquefy 与 liquor。

items.example: The root is about water and light.
Liquid metal poured from the mould.
items.exampleCN: 液态金属从模具中倒出。

items.example: Keep the liquid away from the samples.
Liquidity vanished within hours.
items.exampleCN: 流动性在数小时内消失。

items.example: The gas liquefies under pressure.
Liquefaction destabilized the ground.
The court ordered the firm liquidated.

items.meaning: one who winds up an estate
items.example: The liquidator sold the stock.
Liquor is taxed heavily.
The shares are illiquid.

definition_zh: 烈酒；酒；液体；溶液
definition_en: a strong alcoholic drink made by distillation, alcoholic drink in general, or a liquid used in cooking or in an industrial process
core_image: 高脚杯里琥珀色的酒液轻轻一晃，杯壁上挂着一层薄光
scene: 深夜的柜子里只剩半瓶琥珀色的酒，主人把它倒进小杯。He poured a little liquor into the glass and sat by the fire.
sceneCN: 这里 liquor 是「烈酒」（第 1 个义项：蒸馏得到的烈性酒）；句意为他往杯里倒了一点烈酒，在炉火边坐下。图中可辨识物件：暗色酒柜、琥珀色酒液、炉火。

pos.zh: 烈酒；酒；液体；溶液

derivatives.zh: 由 liquor 加 -ous 构成，义为「酒味浓的；烈性的」，现代多用 alcoholic 替代
由 liquor 与 store 复合，义为「酒类专卖店」，主要用于北美
由 liquor 与 licence 复合，义为「酒类经营许可证」

senses.title: A strong distilled alcoholic drink
senses.definition: a strong alcoholic drink produced by distilling grain, fruit or other material
senses.definitionCN: 用谷物、水果等原料蒸馏而成的烈性酒
senses.example: He poured a little liquor into the glass and sat by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 他往杯里倒了一点烈酒，在炉火边坐下。
senses.why: Latin liquor simply meant fluid, and early English used it for any liquid; distillation produced the strongest drinkable fluid, so the word settled on spirits.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 liquor 本只是「液体」，早期英语也用它指任何液体；蒸馏造出了最强烈的可饮液体，于是这个词落在了烈酒上。

senses.title: Alcoholic drink in general
senses.definition: alcoholic drink of any kind, as the word is used in laws and shops
senses.definitionCN: 任何种类的含酒精饮料，常见于法律与商店用语
senses.example: The state controls where liquor may be sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这个州管制烈酒可以在哪些地方出售。
senses.why: A law has to name the whole category it regulates, so the old word for fluid became the legal label for every drink containing alcohol.
senses.whyCN: 法律必须给它管制的整个类别起个名字，于是那个表示液体的旧词成了所有含酒精饮料的法律标签。

senses.title: The liquid left after cooking
senses.definition: the liquid left in the pot after food has been boiled or stewed
senses.definitionCN: 食物煮或炖之后留在锅里的液体
senses.example: She spooned the pot liquor over the greens.
senses.exampleCN: 她把锅里的汤汁舀到青菜上。
senses.why: Cooks saw the same thing chemists did, a flavoured fluid separated from solid food, and the old general sense of fluid made the name natural.
senses.whyCN: 厨子和化学家看到的是同一件事：从固体食物里分出来的一种有味液体；而 fluid 那个旧义让这个叫法显得再自然不过。

senses.title: A liquid in an industrial process
senses.definition: a liquid used or produced in an industrial or chemical process, such as the mother liquor left after crystals form
senses.definitionCN: 工业或化学过程中使用或产生的液体，如结晶后留下的母液
senses.example: The factory recycles the spent liquor instead of dumping it.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂回收用过的溶液，而不是把它倒掉。
senses.why: Industry needed a plain word for whatever flows through pipes and tanks, and it chose the Latin word for fluid rather than inventing a new term.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要一个朴素的词来指在管道和槽罐里流动的东西，于是选了拉丁语中「液体」那个词，而没有另造新术语。

intro.en: Liquor is a Latin noun for fluid that passed through French and narrowed in English from any liquid to strong drink.
intro.cn: liquor 是拉丁语中表示「液体」的名词，经法语传入英语后，从泛指液体缩小到专指烈酒。

items.en: Liquor was a Latin noun for fluid or liquid, formed from the verb that meant to be liquid.
items.cn: liquor 是拉丁语中表示「液体」的名词，由意为「呈液态」的动词构成。

items.en: The verb liquere meant to be fluid or clear, and it also gave liquidus, the adjective for something flowing.
items.cn: 动词 liquere 意为呈液态、清澈，它还给出了形容词 liquidus，用来描述流动的东西。

items.en: Old French took the word as licor or liquor, naming any liquid and later a drink.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词写作 licor 或 liquor，泛指任何液体，后来也指饮品。

items.en: Middle English liquor could still mean any fluid, not only something to drink.
items.cn: 中古英语的 liquor 仍可指任何液体，而不只是能喝的东西。

items.en: Modern English narrows the everyday sense to strong drink, while chemistry keeps liquor for any liquid in a process.
items.cn: 现代英语把日常义项缩小到烈酒，而化学仍用 liquor 指工艺过程中的任何液体。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of flowing and being liquid; the near-meaning group gathers words for alcohol and strong drink.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中「流动、呈液态」的词干展开；近义组收表示酒精与烈酒的词。

entries.definition: A substance that flows and is not solid.
entries.definitionCN: 液体；与 liquor 同出拉丁语 liquere。

entries.definition: To turn something into a liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 使液化；由同一拉丁词干加 -fy 构成。

entries.definition: A sweet alcoholic drink served after a meal.
entries.definitionCN: 餐后甜酒；与 liquor 同出拉丁语 liquor，但经法语单独借入。

entries.definition: A sweet root used in sweets and medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 甘草；拼写与 liquor 相近，但词源来自希腊语，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The chemical in drinks that makes people drunk, or drink in general.
entries.definitionCN: 酒精；也泛指含酒精饮料。

entries.definition: Strong distilled alcoholic drinks.
entries.definitionCN: 烈酒；蒸馏酒。

entries.definition: A strong alcoholic drink distilled from wine.
entries.definitionCN: 白兰地；由葡萄酒蒸馏而成的烈酒。

entries.definition: Alcohol, especially in large amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 酒；口语说法，常指大量饮酒。

normalIntro.en: The word begins as a Latin name for anything fluid, and its family keeps returning to flow, clarity and the strongest drink.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是拉丁语中泛指液体的名字，它的同族词反复回到流动、清澈以及最烈的酒。

normal.en: Latin liquor is simply fluid, and the word entered English as a general name for anything that flows.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 liquor 就是「液体」，这个词进入英语时是泛指一切流动之物的名字。

normal.en: The Latin verb liquere means to be liquid or clear, and it also gave the adjective liquidus.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 liquere 意为呈液态、清澈，它还给出了形容词 liquidus。

normal.en: Old French kept the word as licor for any liquid, and English narrowed the everyday sense to drink.
normal.cn: 古法语把这个词保留为 licor，泛指任何液体；英语把日常义项缩小到了饮品。

normal.en: Distillation concentrates alcohol into the strongest fluid a still can produce, so liquor came to mean spirits.
normal.cn: 蒸馏把酒精浓缩成蒸馏器能造出的最强烈液体，于是 liquor 逐渐指烈酒。

normal.en: Mother liquor is the liquid left around crystals, so the same word still serves chemistry and the bar.
normal.cn: 母液是结晶之后留在晶体周围的液体，所以同一个词至今同时服务于化学实验室和酒吧。

abstract.en: A fluid takes the shape of whatever holds it, which is why liquor can name a drink, a bath and a broth without strain.
abstract.cn: 液体随容器改变形状，所以 liquor 能毫不费力地指一杯酒、一槽液体或一锅汤汁。

abstract.en: Alcohol is a liquid that burns, and the word carries both the cool flow and the hidden heat.
abstract.cn: 酒精是一种会燃烧的液体，这个词同时装着流动的凉意和藏起来的热。

abstract.en: Every language needs a plain word for what pours, and liquor is English's oldest answer.
abstract.cn: 每种语言都需要一个朴素的词来指会倾倒的东西，liquor 就是英语最老的答案。

examples.en: He poured a little liquor into the glass and sat by the fire.
examples.cn: 他往杯里倒了一点烈酒，在炉火边坐下。

examples.en: The state controls where liquor may be sold.
examples.cn: 这个州管制烈酒可以在哪些地方出售。

examples.en: The factory recycles the spent liquor instead of dumping it.
examples.cn: 这家工厂回收用过的溶液，而不是把它倒掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立刻」——烈酒一入口，人立刻就上了头；liquor 是烈酒，也是会流动的液体。

root: 拉丁语 liquor（液体）来自动词 liquere（呈液态、清澈），经古法语 licur 进入英语；同族词多与流动、液体、清澈有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a clear flowing fluid; from it come the distilled drink, the legal category of alcohol, the cooking broth and the industrial bath.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种清澈流动的液体；由此分出蒸馏酒、法律上的酒类、锅里的汤汁，以及工业用的溶液。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: amber liquid swaying in a glass, leaving a thin film of light on the wall.

definition_en: the metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre, a quantity of that size, or the same unit used for engine displacement
core_image: 透明量杯里，液面停在标着升数的刻度上
scene: 厨房里，厨师把牛奶倒进量杯，瓶身上的容量标注正好对齐刻度。A single liter of milk was enough for the whole batter.
sceneCN: 这里 liter 是「一升的量」（第 2 个义项：按升计的一份液体）；句意是一升牛奶就够和这一整盆面糊。画面里可抓住的物件：量杯、瓶身容量标注、对齐的刻度。

pos.zh: 升（公制容积单位）；一升的量；以升计的排量

senses.title: The metric unit of volume
senses.definition: the metric unit of volume equal to one cubic decimetre, used for liquids, gases, and loose dry goods
senses.definitionCN: 公制容积单位，等于一立方分米，用于液体、气体以及松散干物
senses.example: The tank holds forty liters of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个水箱能装四十升水。
senses.why: The word entered English together with the metric system, which gave volume a decimal unit; a litre is defined as the space inside a cube ten centimetres on each side, so the size is fixed by geometry rather than by any bottle.
senses.whyCN: 这个词随公制一起进入英语，公制为容积设定了十进制的单位；一升定义为一个十厘米见方的立方体内部的容积，因此大小由几何确定，而不是由某个瓶子决定。

senses.title: A quantity of that size, especially of a drink or fuel
senses.titleCN: 一升的量：按升卖的一份
senses.definition: a quantity of liquid amounting to one liter, especially as sold or poured
senses.definitionCN: 等于一升的液体量，尤指售卖或倒出的一份
senses.example: He bought a liter of milk on the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 他回家路上买了一升牛奶。
senses.why: Once the unit is fixed, it can count portions instead of only measuring them; shopkeepers and cooks say a liter of milk the way others say a bottle or a cup, and the unit takes a plural.
senses.whyCN: 单位一旦固定，就可以用来数「份」而不只是测量；店家与厨师说一升牛奶，就像别人说一瓶、一杯，这个单位也就能变复数。

senses.title: A unit for engine displacement
senses.titleCN: 排量：以升计的气缸容积
senses.definition: the same unit used to state the total volume swept by the pistons of an engine, as in a two-liter engine
senses.definitionCN: 同一单位用于表示发动机活塞扫过的总容积，如「两升发动机」
senses.example: The car has a small one-liter engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车配的是一台小型一升发动机。
senses.why: Engine size is itself a volume, so the same unit travels from the kitchen to the garage; a two-liter engine is an engine whose cylinders sweep two liters of air in one cycle.
senses.whyCN: 发动机排量本身就是容积，所以同一单位从厨房走进车库；两升发动机就是气缸在一个循环里扫过两升空气的发动机。

intro.en: Liter came into English through French from a Latin borrowing of a Greek unit name; the American spelling dropped the British re ending.
intro.cn: liter 经法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语对希腊单位名的借用；美式拼写省去了英式的 re 词尾。

items.en: The Greek word litra named a Sicilian unit of weight and, by extension, of capacity; its own earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 litra 指西西里的一种重量单位，也引申指容量单位；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as litra, still a unit of weight, and passed it on to the languages of western Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 litra，仍作重量单位，并把它传进西欧诸语言。

items.en: Old French used litre for a measure of capacity, and French kept the word when the metric system was created.
items.cn: 古法语用 litre 表示一种容量单位，法国在创立公制时保留了这个词。

items.en: English adopted litre along with metric measures in the nineteenth century, spelled in the French way.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪随公制一起引入 litre，并按法语方式拼写。

items.en: American usage settled on liter, while British usage keeps litre; compounds such as milliliter and kiloliter follow the American form in the United States.
items.cn: 美式用法定型为 liter，英式仍作 litre；milliliter、kiloliter 等复合词在美国跟随美式写法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the British spelling and near spellings with different histories; the near-meaning group collects other units and words for volume.
note.cn: 形近组收英式拼写与历史无关的近似拼写；近义组收其他单位以及表示容积的词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same unit, with no difference in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 同一单位的英式拼写，含义没有差别。

entries.definition: A written symbol or a written message; it is only close in spelling, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 字母或信件；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A unit of length, or a measuring device; the spelling is close but the word is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 长度单位或计量仪表；拼写相近，但词源无关。

entries.definition: One thousandth of a liter.
entries.definitionCN: 千分之一升；毫升。

entries.definition: A larger unit of liquid volume used in Britain and America.
entries.definitionCN: 英美使用的一种较大液体容量单位。

entries.definition: A quarter of a gallon, used for milk and other liquids.
entries.definitionCN: 四分之一加仑，用于牛奶等液体。

entries.definition: A smaller unit of liquid volume, about half a quart.
entries.definitionCN: 较小的液体容量单位，约半夸脱。

entries.definition: The amount of space that something occupies.
entries.definitionCN: 物体所占空间的大小；体积。

normalIntro.en: The word arrived through Greek, Latin and French already carrying a measuring habit, and its spelling split between litre and liter.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词经希腊语、拉丁语和法语传来时已经带着测量的习惯，后来拼写在 litre 与 liter 之间分家。

normal.en: The Greek unit litra came through Latin and French, so the word arrived already carrying a measuring habit.
normal.cn: 希腊单位 litra 经拉丁语和法语传来，所以这个词到达英语时已经带着测量的习惯。

normal.en: Liter and litre are the same unit; only the ending differs between American and British spelling.
normal.cn: liter 与 litre 是同一个单位，只是美式与英式拼写的词尾不同。

normal.en: Milliliter puts milli-, one thousandth, in front of liter, so the unit shrinks by three decimal places.
normal.cn: milliliter 在 liter 前加表示千分之一的 milli-，单位缩小了三位小数。

normal.en: Kiloliter adds kilo-, one thousand, at the other end of the scale.
normal.cn: kiloliter 在刻度另一端加上表示一千的 kilo-。

normal.en: Because a liter is a volume, the same word measures milk, petrol and the cylinders of an engine.
normal.cn: 既然升是容积，同一个词就能量牛奶、汽油和发动机气缸。

abstract.en: A unit is a promise that everyone will cut the world the same way.
abstract.cn: 单位是一种承诺：所有人都用同样的方式切割世界。

abstract.en: Decimal measures travel easily because each step is a power of ten, which is why liter fits so neatly with milli- and kilo-.
abstract.cn: 十进制的度量容易传播，因为每一步都是十的幂，所以 liter 与 milli-、kilo- 配合得严丝合缝。

abstract.en: The same liter can sit in a kitchen, a fuel pump or an engine bay, and the number stays comparable.
abstract.cn: 同一升可以出现在厨房、油泵或发动机舱，数字始终可比。

examples.cn: 他回家路上买了一升牛奶。

examples.en: The car has a one-liter engine.

sensesIntro.en: The core is one metric unit of volume; it extends to a poured quantity, and then to engine size, which is measured in the same unit.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个公制容积单位；它延伸到倒出的一份液体，再延伸到同样以容积计量的发动机排量。

intro.cn: 这个词是一串借用：从希腊单位经拉丁语、法语到两种现代拼写，再由公制前缀造出更大和更小的单位。
