definition_zh: 读写能力；（某一领域的）基本素养与判断力；识字普及程度
definition_en: the ability to read and write, and the competence needed to understand and use information in a particular field
core_image: 一张旧书桌上摊开的识字课本，页边压着一支削短的铅笔，旁边是一份签过名字的登记表
scene: 夜校的桌上摊着识字课本，页边压着一支削短的铅笔。Adult literacy classes fill the church hall on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
sceneCN: 这里指「读写能力」（第 1 个义项：读书识字的基本能力）；句意为成人识字班每逢周二和周四坐满了教堂大厅。可辨识物件：识字课本、铅笔、登记表、长桌。

pos.zh: 读写能力；素养（通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 识字的；有文化的 / 识字者

senses.title: The ability to read and write
senses.definition: the basic ability to read and write a short simple text
senses.definitionCN: 读懂并写出简短浅近文字的基本能力
senses.example: Literacy opens the first door that poverty had shut.
senses.exampleCN: 读写能力打开了贫困关上的第一道门。
senses.why: the noun was built on the Latin word for a letter of the alphabet, so its oldest content is simply knowing one's letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建在拉丁语「字母」一词上，因此它最古老的内容就是「认识字母」。

senses.title: The measured level in a population
senses.titleCN: 一个人群中被统计的识字程度
senses.definition: the share of a population that can read and write, treated as a figure to be counted
senses.definitionCN: 能够读写者在人口中所占的比例，被当作可统计的数字
senses.example: Literacy in the province rose from half to four fifths in one generation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个省的识字水平在一代人之内从一半升至五分之四。
senses.why: once states began to measure the skill, the word also named the number rather than the ability.
senses.whyCN: 一旦国家开始测量这项技能，这个词也就指数字而非能力。

senses.title: Functional literacy for daily tasks
senses.titleCN: 应付日常事务的实用读写能力
senses.definition: the reading and writing needed to fill in forms, follow instructions and manage a household
senses.definitionCN: 填写表格、看懂指示、料理家务所需的读写能力
senses.example: The course targets functional literacy rather than exam skills.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课针对的是日常实用读写能力，而不是应试技巧。
senses.why: policy shifted focus from letters to use, so the old word acquired a practical measure.
senses.whyCN: 政策重心从「认字」转向「会用」，这个旧词由此带上实用尺度。

senses.title: Digital literacy
senses.titleCN: 使用数字工具与判断网络信息的能力
senses.definition: the ability to use computers and networks and to judge what one finds there
senses.definitionCN: 使用计算机与网络，并判断所见信息的能力
senses.example: Students need digital literacy before they can research online.
senses.exampleCN: 学生要先具备数字素养，才能在网络上做研究。
senses.why: the pattern of basic competence in a domain was extended from print to screens.
senses.whyCN: 「某领域的基本能力」这一模式从纸面扩展到了屏幕。

senses.title: Financial literacy
senses.titleCN: 看懂收支、利率与风险的能力
senses.definition: the ability to understand money, interest, debt and risk well enough to decide wisely
senses.definitionCN: 理解金钱、利率、债务与风险并据以明智决策的能力
senses.example: Schools now teach financial literacy alongside mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 学校如今把金融素养与数学一起教。
senses.why: the same frame applies wherever a field has codes that outsiders cannot read.
senses.whyCN: 只要某领域有一套外人读不懂的规则，这个框架就适用。

senses.title: Media literacy
senses.titleCN: 识别媒体信息意图与可信度的能力
senses.definition: the ability to read how news and advertising are built, and to judge their reliability
senses.definitionCN: 看懂新闻与广告如何被构造，并判断其可信度的能力
senses.example: Media literacy helps readers notice what a headline leaves out.
senses.exampleCN: 媒体素养帮助读者察觉标题省略了什么。
senses.why: news and advertising are constructed texts, so reading them needs the same skill as reading print.
senses.whyCN: 新闻与广告都是被构造的文本，读懂它们需要与读印刷品相同的功夫。

senses.title: Cultural literacy
senses.titleCN: 共享文化常识的通晓程度
senses.definition: the shared background knowledge that lets people understand references and jokes
senses.definitionCN: 使人能理解典故与玩笑的共同背景知识
senses.example: Cultural literacy includes knowing why a certain date matters.
senses.exampleCN: 文化素养包括知道某个日期为何重要。
senses.why: the word widened from letters to the common stock of references a society assumes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「字母」扩展到社会默认人人共有的典故储备。

senses.title: Literacy in a specialized field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业领域的基本通晓
senses.definition: working knowledge of the basic ideas and vocabulary of a subject such as science or law
senses.definitionCN: 对科学、法律等学科的基本概念与术语具备可用知识
senses.example: Scientific literacy is now treated as part of general education.
senses.exampleCN: 科学素养如今被视为通识教育的一部分。
senses.why: a subject's basic vocabulary works like an alphabet, so the same word fits it.
senses.whyCN: 某学科的基本词汇就像一套字母，因此同一个词也适用于它。

intro.en: Literacy is English literate plus the noun ending -cy, and literate goes back to Latin litteratus 'lettered', built on littera 'letter of the alphabet'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词是在英语形容词「识字的」上加名词后缀构成，而该形容词上溯拉丁 litteratus「识字的」，后者建于 littera「字母」之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet; in the plural it also meant a written message or writings in general. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母；复数时也指书信或一般著作。其更深来源未获证明。

items.en: Litteratus meant 'marked with letters, lettered, learned', an adjective formed from the noun.
items.cn: litteratus 意为「写有字母的、识字的、有学问的」，是由该名词构成的形容词。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective in the fifteenth century, using it first for learned people and later for anyone able to read.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，先用于有学问的人，后用于任何能读书的人。

items.en: The noun is a nineteenth-century formation, made as the positive counterpart of illiteracy when mass schooling made the skill a public question.
items.cn: 这个名词是十九世纪的构词，作为「文盲状态」的反面说法而造，当时大众教育使识字成为公共议题。

items.en: From the late twentieth century the word was attached to new fields, giving digital, financial, media and scientific literacy.
items.cn: 从二十世纪后期起，这个词被挂到新的领域上，形成数字、金融、媒体与科学素养等说法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the word for a letter is unknown, and the exact first printed use of the modern noun is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，这个现代名词最早的确切印刷书证亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same letter-root that are easily swapped; group two holds neighbours naming competence.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「字母」词根、容易用错的词；第二组是表示能力的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes a person or society that can read; the noun names the ability itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能读写的个人或社会；名词则指能力本身。

entries.definition: The body of written works, or the published material on a subject; it is the product, not the ability.
entries.definitionCN: 指成体系的著作，或某主题的已发表文献；是产物而非能力。

entries.definition: Meaning 'following the exact words'; it shares the letter-root but has nothing to do with reading skill.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「照字面的」，虽共享「字母」词根，却与读写能力无关。

entries.definition: The lack of the ability; it is the negative noun built with a prefix of negation.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏这种能力，是用否定前缀构成的反面名词。

entries.definition: Basic competence with numbers, coined on the model of literacy.
entries.definitionCN: 指对数字的基本能力，仿照「读写能力」造出。

entries.definition: The broad process of schooling; literacy is one measurable part of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛的学校教育过程；读写能力是其中可测量的一部分。

entries.definition: A general word for a high level of skill in something; it carries no link to letters.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某项技能的高水平，不含与「字母」的联系。

entries.definition: The sufficiency to perform a task; it is broader and less measurable than literacy.
entries.definitionCN: 指足以完成任务的能力，范围更广，且不如读写能力那样可测量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'letter', so the core of the word is literally knowing one's letters.
normal.cn: 词根意为「字母」，因此这个词的核心字面上就是「认识字母」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the newer fields: digital, financial and media literacy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出较新的领域：数字素养、金融素养与媒体素养。

normal.en: The noun pairs with its negative twin, one built with a prefix of denial.
normal.cn: 这个名词与它的否定孪生词配对，后者由否定前缀构成。

normal.en: The family runs literate, illiterate, literature, literal, literacy.
normal.cn: 同族包括「识字的」「不识字的」「文学」「字面的」「读写能力」。

normal.en: The phrase 'literacy campaign' keeps the public-policy sense visible.
normal.cn: 「扫盲运动」这一说法让公共政策义保持可见。

abstract.en: Picture a key that fits many doors but was cut for one lock first.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能开许多门的钥匙，最初却只为一把锁而削。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that lets a reader walk through a dark room without falling.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯，让读者走过暗室而不摔倒。

abstract.en: Picture a currency accepted in every shop, learned one letter at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一种每个店铺都收的货币，是一个字母一个字母学来的。

examples.en: Literacy among women rose fastest where evening classes were free.
examples.cn: 在夜校免费的地方，女性识字率上升最快。

examples.en: Digital literacy is now as basic as reading a timetable.
examples.cn: 数字素养如今已和看懂时刻表一样基础。

examples.en: The campaign cut adult illiteracy by half in six years.
examples.cn: 这场运动在六年内把成人文盲率降低了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特乐西」——里里外外认得那些特小的字母，心里就乐，这就是读写能力。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」构成形容词 litteratus「识字的」；英语先借入形容词，十九世纪再加名词后缀构成 literacy，作为「文盲状态」的反面说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one seed: knowing letters becomes the ability to read, then a number to count, then a set of practical competences that spread to screens, money, news and finally to any field with its own codes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一粒种子长出：认识字母变成读写能力，再变成可统计的数字，随后成为一套实用能力，扩展到屏幕、金钱、新闻，最后延伸到任何有自身规则的专业领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short pencil pressed on a page beside a signed form.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支削短的铅笔压在纸页上，旁边是一份签过名的表格。

branches.en: THE SEED: knowing letters is the oldest and simplest layer of the word.
branches.cn: 种子：认识字母是这个词最古老也最简单的一层。

branches.en: COUNTED: a state can turn the ability into a percentage, and the word follows.
branches.cn: 被计数：国家能把能力换算成百分比，词义也随之跟进。

branches.en: USING IT: forms and instructions on one side, a discipline's vocabulary on the other.
branches.cn: 会用：一边是表格与说明，另一边是某学科的专业词汇。

branches.en: NEW MEDIA: screens and headlines each demand a literacy of their own.
branches.cn: 新媒介：屏幕与标题各自要求一套自己的素养。

branches.en: CODES OF THE WORLD: money and shared culture are also systems one must learn to read.
branches.cn: 世界的密码：金钱与共同文化同样是必须学会读懂的体系。

intro.en: The word is a short English noun built on a Latin root for a letter, with a suffix of state or quality.
intro.cn: 这是一个简短的英语名词，建在拉丁语表「字母」的词根上，并带一个表状态或性质的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera gives letter, letters and literature in English, while litteratus gives literate and, with a negating prefix, illiterate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 在英语里衍生出「字母」「书信」与「文学」，litteratus 则衍生出「识字的」，加上否定前缀又有「不识字的」。

items.meaning: a letter; writings in the plural
items.meaningCN: 字母；复数指书信或著作
items.example: The root names the smallest unit of written language.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指书面语言的最小单位。

items.meaning: a written sign for a speech sound
items.example: A single letter can change a whole meaning.
items.exampleCN: 一个字母就能改变整个意思。

items.example: The village is almost wholly literate now.
items.exampleCN: 这个村子如今几乎人人识字。

items.meaning: the state of being able to read
items.example: Literacy was made a national target.
The forms were useless to illiterate tenants.
items.exampleCN: 这些表格对不识字的租户毫无用处。

items.example: She read the literature on soil erosion.
items.exampleCN: 她读了关于土壤侵蚀的文献。

items.example: A literal translation missed the joke.
He was a man of letters in the old sense.
items.exampleCN: 在旧时的意义上，他是个文人。

definition_zh: 按字面；逐字地；确实地；简直（口语夸张用法）
definition_en: in a literal sense or word for word, in fact, or, informally, as a strong intensifier with little literal truth
core_image: 手指沿着印刷的一行字，一个字母一个字母移过去
scene: 朋友把一句玩笑当成真话，还认真追问细节，旁边的人忍不住笑。She took his joke literally and began checking the figures.
sceneCN: 这里 literally 是「按字面」（第 1 个义项：照词语本义理解）；句意是她把玩笑按字面当真，开始核对数字。画面里可抓住的动作：朋友认真追问、旁人的笑、纸上待核对的数字。

pos.zh: 按字面；逐字地；确实地；简直

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 littera（字母）加 -al 构成，指字面的、照字面理解的
由 literal 加 -ness 构成，指拘泥字面的性质
由 literal 加 -ism 构成，指拘泥字面、字面主义的做法
由 literal 加 -ist 构成，指死抠字面的人

senses.title: In the literal sense of the words
senses.titleCN: 按字面：照词语本来的意思
senses.definition: in the ordinary, literal meaning of the words used, rather than in a figurative or exaggerated one
senses.definitionCN: 按所用词语的本义去理解，而不是按比喻或夸张的意思
senses.example: The phrase was meant literally, not as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话是按字面意思说的，不是开玩笑。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet, so literally begins as 'according to the letters': you read what the words actually say, and no picture is allowed to stand in for them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语 littera（字母）之上，literally 的起点是「按照字母」：你读的是词语实际写出的内容，不许任何比喻顶替它。

senses.title: Word for word
senses.definition: word for word, following the exact order and wording of the original
senses.definitionCN: 逐字照原话的顺序与措辞，不作改动
senses.example: The contract was translated literally, so the jokes disappeared.
senses.exampleCN: 合同是逐字翻译的，所以笑话全没了。
senses.why: If you follow the letters one by one, you also follow the words in their original order; translation done this way keeps the surface and loses the idiom.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个字母一个字母地跟着走，也就按原来的顺序跟着词走；这样翻译保住了表面，却丢掉了习语。

senses.title: In fact, really
senses.titleCN: 确实地：强调事情真的发生
senses.definition: actually, really, without exaggeration, used to stress that something surprising is true
senses.definitionCN: 确实、真的，不带夸张，用来强调某件令人意外的事是真的
senses.example: The team literally ran out of paper on the last day.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在最后一天确实把纸用完了。
senses.why: Because 'according to the letters' means 'according to the facts as stated', the adverb can certify a statement: what sounds like an exaggeration is being claimed as plain truth.
senses.whyCN: 既然「按字面」就是「按写明的事实」，这个副词就能为陈述作证：听起来像夸张的话，其实是在说大实话。

senses.title: As an intensifier, almost
senses.titleCN: 口语夸张用法：简直、几乎（并不字面）
senses.definition: used in informal speech as a strong intensifier, often when the statement is not literally true
senses.definitionCN: 口语中作强烈的加强词，常用于所述并非字面真实的情况
senses.example: I literally died laughing at that video.
senses.exampleCN: 那个视频简直把我笑死了。
senses.why: Intensifiers wear out and are borrowed from stronger words; speakers reached for literally to mark emphasis, and the very word for exactness became a badge of exaggeration, a usage dictionaries now record.
senses.whyCN: 加强词会磨损，于是从更有力的词里借用；说话人抓来 literally 表示强调，结果这个专管精确的词反倒成了夸张的标记，词典如今已收录这种用法。

intro.en: Literally is an English adverb built on literal, which descends from Latin littera, a letter of the alphabet.
intro.cn: literally 是英语副词，建立在 literal 之上，而 literal 源自拉丁语 littera（字母）。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural litterae it could mean a letter, a document, or learning.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数 litterae 可指书信、文书或学问。

items.en: Late Latin litteralis meant 'of letters' and described meaning that stays with the written words.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 litteralis 意为「字母的」，用来描述紧贴字面文字的涵义。

items.en: English took literal in the fifteenth century for meaning that follows the letter rather than the spirit.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪引入 literal，指跟随字面而非精神的理解。

items.en: Literally was formed with -ly soon after, first for word-for-word rendering and then for stating plain fact.
items.cn: literally 随后由 -ly 构成，先表逐字表达，再表陈述直白的事实。

items.en: In the twentieth century the intensifier use spread in speech, and it is now recorded, though still criticised in formal writing.
items.cn: 二十世纪里，加强语气的用法在口语中扩散，如今已被收录，但在正式写作中仍有争议。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for letter; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of exactness and reality.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「字母」词干上的词；近义组收表示精确与真实的副词。

entries.definition: Following the basic meaning of the words.
entries.definitionCN: 按词语本义的；字面的。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write, built on the same stem for letters.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力，同样建立在「字母」词干上。

entries.definition: Written works, from the same stem as letters.
entries.definitionCN: 文学作品，与「字母」同一词干。

entries.definition: A written symbol or message, from the same Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 字母或书信，来自同一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: Relating to literature or written language.
entries.definitionCN: 与文学或书面语言有关的。

entries.definition: In a precise way, with nothing added or left out.
entries.definitionCN: 精确地，不增不减。

entries.definition: In fact, as opposed to what was expected.
entries.definitionCN: 事实上，与预期相对。

entries.definition: In a genuine or sincere way.
entries.definitionCN: 真正地；真诚地。

entries.definition: In effect or almost, though not strictly.
entries.definitionCN: 实际上；几乎，虽非严格如此。

normalIntro.en: Literal comes from a Latin noun for a letter, so the adverb is a word about reading the letters in front of you.
normalIntro.cn: literal 来自拉丁语中表示字母的名词，所以这个副词是一个关于「读眼前字母」的词。

normal.en: Literal comes from littera, a letter, so a literal reading stays with the letters in front of you.
normal.cn: literal 来自 littera（字母），所以字面阅读就是紧跟着眼前的字母。

normal.en: Add -ly and the adjective becomes the adverb that says how the reading is done.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly，形容词就变成说明「怎样读」的副词。

normal.en: Translate literally is word for word; translate freely is by sense, and the two labels mark opposite choices.
normal.cn: 逐字翻译是跟着词走，意译是跟着意思走，两个说法标出相反的选择。

normal.en: Literally true certifies a surprising fact, so the word is doing the work of really.
normal.cn: literally true 是在为一件意外的事实作证，这个词在做 really 的活。

normal.en: A sentence like I literally died is not literal at all, which shows the intensifier has drifted from its root.
normal.cn: 像「我简直死了」这样的句子一点也不是字面意思，可见这个加强词已经漂离了词根。

abstract.en: A word built on letters becomes a word for truth, and then for emphasis, and the direction of travel is worth noticing.
abstract.cn: 一个建立在字母上的词变成了表示真实的词，又变成加强词，这个移动方向值得注意。

abstract.en: Exactness is a surface; when a sentence is read only at the surface, the joke or the metaphor is lost.
abstract.cn: 精确只是表面；只按表面读一句话，玩笑或隐喻就丢了。

abstract.en: The strongest claim of literalness can end up producing the least literal sentence.
abstract.cn: 最卖力声称字面的一句话，可能恰恰最不字面。

examples.en: The phrase was meant literally, not as a joke.
examples.cn: 这句话是按字面意思说的，不是玩笑。

examples.en: The contract was translated literally.
examples.cn: 这份合同是逐字翻译的。

examples.en: The team literally ran out of paper.
examples.cn: 团队确实把纸用完了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「李特柔利」——把每个字都照原样读出来，literally 是字面地。

root: 拉丁语 littera（字母）→ 晚期拉丁语 litteralis（字母的；字面的）→ 英语 literal → 加 -ly 成 literally；核心义「按字面」，后发展出「确实」与口语夸张用法。

sensesIntro.en: The core is reading by the letters; it branches into word-for-word rendering, into certifying plain fact, and into the looser intensifier use of speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是照着字母读；由此分出逐字翻译、为事实作证，以及口语里较松的夸张加强用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger moving letter by letter across a line of print.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指沿着印刷的一行字，一个字母一个字母地移过去。

branches.en: a reader stopping at the exact words on the page
branches.cn: 读者停在页面上确切的词句

branches.en: a translator following the original word by word
branches.cn: 译者逐词跟着原文

branches.en: a report confirming that the shortage was real
branches.cn: 报告确认短缺确有其事

branches.en: a friend insisting that the exaggeration really happened
branches.cn: 朋友坚称那句夸张的话真发生过

branches.en: the gap between the word and what it now claims
branches.cn: 词与它如今声称的东西之间的缝

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin noun for a letter, a Late Latin adjective, and two English suffixes that make an adjective and an adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示字母的拉丁语名词、晚期拉丁语形容词，以及构成形容词与副词的两个英语后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun littera and its derivative adjective litteralis supply the whole family, and English keeps the stem in literal, literary and literature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 littera 及其派生形容词 litteralis 提供了整族词，英语在 literal、literary 与 literature 里保留了这一词干。

latinEntries.meaning: a letter of the alphabet; in the plural, a letter or literature
latinEntries.meaningCN: 字母；复数可指书信或文献

definition_zh: 识字的；有文化的；通晓某领域的（也可作名词：识字的人）
definition_en: able to read and write, educated, or knowledgeable about a particular subject
core_image: 一位老人坐在窗边的木桌前，手指按着一页密密麻麻的文字，桌角摞着几本翻旧的书
scene: 窗边的木桌前，一位老人用手指按着一页密密麻麻的文字，桌上摞着翻旧的书。By eighty she was still a keen reader, wholly literate and never without a book.
sceneCN: 这里指「具备读写能力」（第 1 个义项：能够读书写字）；句意为她到八十岁仍爱读书，完全识字，手边从不缺书。可辨识物件：木桌、书页、旧书、窗光。

pos.zh: 识字的；有文化的；通晓的
识字的人；有文化的人（较少用）

senses.title: Able to read and write
senses.definition: having the basic ability to read and write simple texts
senses.definitionCN: 具备读懂并写出浅近文字的基本能力
senses.example: Only half the adults in the district were literate in nineteen fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 一九五零年，这个区只有一半成年人识字。
senses.why: the adjective is the direct Latin word for 'lettered', so its first sense is the plain possession of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接来自拉丁语「写有字母的」，因此第一义就是字面意义上的「认得字母」。

senses.title: Educated and well read
senses.definition: having a broad education and familiarity with serious writing
senses.definitionCN: 受过良好教育并熟悉严肃著作
senses.example: Her letters show a literate mind at work.
senses.exampleCN: 她的书信显出一个有教养的心灵在运转。
senses.why: knowing letters grew into knowing books, and knowing books grew into general cultivation.
senses.whyCN: 「认得字母」长成「读过书」，「读过书」又长成「有教养」。

senses.title: Functionally literate in daily life
senses.titleCN: 能应付日常事务的书信能力
senses.definition: able to handle forms, instructions and ordinary paperwork without help
senses.definitionCN: 无需他人帮助即可处理表格、说明与日常文书
senses.example: Applicants must be functionally literate to fill the form alone.
senses.exampleCN: 申请人须具备实用读写能力，才能独立填表。
senses.why: administration turned the broad ability into a practical threshold.
senses.whyCN: 行政事务把宽泛的能力变成一个实用门槛。

senses.title: Computer literate
senses.titleCN: 会用计算机与常用软件
senses.definition: confident with computers and common software, usually in the fixed phrase computer literate
senses.definitionCN: 能熟练使用计算机与常用软件，通常见于「会用电脑」这一固定说法
senses.example: New staff must be computer literate before they start.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工入职前必须会用电脑。
senses.why: a computer's keyboard and menus became the new letters, so the old adjective was reused.
senses.whyCN: 计算机的键盘与菜单成了新的「字母」，这个旧形容词因此被复用。

senses.title: Literate in a subject
senses.definition: knowing enough of a subject's language to read and judge its material
senses.definitionCN: 掌握某学科的语言，足以阅读并判断其材料
senses.example: Voters should be economically literate enough to read a budget.
senses.exampleCN: 选民应具备足够的经济素养，能读懂一份预算。
senses.why: the pattern 'knows the letters of a field' is reused for every specialty.
senses.whyCN: 「认得某领域的字母」这一模式被复用到每一门专业上。

senses.title: A literate style of writing
senses.definition: describing prose that is clear, polished and clearly the work of a reader
senses.definitionCN: 形容文字清楚、打磨过、明显出自读书人之手
senses.example: The report was literate without being showy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告写得有文气，却不炫耀。
senses.why: the adjective can describe the product as well as the person, because style was seen as the mark of letters.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也能形容作品而非人，因为文风被视为读书的印记。

senses.title: A largely literate population
senses.definition: describing a society or group in which most adults can read and write
senses.definitionCN: 描述多数成年人都能读写的群体或社会
senses.example: A literate workforce adapted quickly to printed instructions.
senses.exampleCN: 识字的劳动力能迅速适应书面说明。
senses.why: the adjective can describe a whole population, because it was originally a description of persons.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最初描述个人，因此也能描述整个人口。

senses.title: A person who can read (noun use)
senses.definition: a person who has learned to read and write, especially in accounts of schooling
senses.definitionCN: 已学会读写的人，尤见于教育记述中
senses.example: The program graduated eight hundred literates in its first year.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目第一年培养出八百名识字者。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun for the people who bear the quality.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词直接用作名词，指具备该性质的人。

intro.en: Literate comes from Latin litteratus 'marked with letters, learned', an adjective on littera 'letter'. English borrowed it in the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁 litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」，该形容词建于 littera「字母」之上，十五世纪进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Littera named a letter of the alphabet, and in the plural a letter, a document or writings. The deeper origin of the word is not established.
items.cn: littera 指字母，复数指书信、文书或著作。这个词更深的来源未获证明。

items.en: The ending -atus formed adjectives of possession, so litteratus meant 'furnished with letters', hence able to read and, by extension, learned.
items.cn: 表「具有」的拉丁形容词词尾构成这类形容词，因此 litteratus 意为「带有字母的」，引申为能读书，再引申为有学问。

items.en: English took the adjective in the fifteenth century, at first describing clergy and scholars rather than ordinary readers.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个形容词，最初描述神职人员与学者，而非普通读者。

items.en: With mass printing and schooling the word spread to anyone who could read, and to whole populations.
items.cn: 随着大众印刷与学校教育普及，这个词扩展到任何能读书的人，也用于整个人口。

items.en: Late twentieth-century usage produced computer literate and financially literate, applying the adjective to specific competences.
items.cn: 二十世纪后期的用法产生了「会用电脑的」「懂金融的」等说法，把这个形容词用于具体能力。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of the letter-word is unknown, and no single first recorded use of the modern everyday sense can be verified.
items.cn: 来源不确定：那个表「字母」的词在拉丁语之前的来源不明，现代日常义的最早书证亦无法确证。

note.en: Group one holds words and forms from the same root that are often confused; group two holds adjectives describing an educated person.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而常被混淆的词形；第二组是描述受教育者的形容词。

entries.definition: The ability itself, not the person who has it; it is what a literate person possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 指能力本身，而非拥有能力的人；它是识字者所拥有的东西。

entries.definition: Meaning 'word for word'; it looks close but describes translation, not reading ability.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「逐字的」，外形接近，却描述翻译方式而非读写能力。

entries.definition: Relating to literature as an art; a literate person need not be literary.
entries.definitionCN: 指与作为艺术的文学有关；识字的人未必有文学趣味。

entries.definition: Unable to read or write; it is the exact opposite, built with a prefix of denial.
entries.definitionCN: 指不能读写，是它的确切反义，由否定前缀构成。

entries.definition: Having had formal schooling; it says nothing about the bare ability to read.
entries.definitionCN: 指受过正规学校教育，不涉及最基本的读写能力。

entries.definition: An older word for widely read and scholarly; it is close in meaning but dated in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧的说法，指博览而博学，意思接近但语气古旧。

entries.definition: Having read widely in serious books; it is narrower than a general literate upbringing.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛读过严肃书籍，范围比一般「有文化」窄。

entries.definition: Comfortable with numbers and quantitative reasoning, coined on the model of literate.
entries.definitionCN: 指熟悉数字与定量推理，仿「识字的」造出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The ending means 'furnished with', so the word literally says a person is furnished with letters.
normal.cn: 那个词尾意为「带有」，因此这个词字面上是说一个人「带着字母」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases add the specialty: computer literate, financially literate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配补上专业领域：会用电脑、懂金融。

normal.en: The positive and negative forms differ only by a prefix of denial.
normal.cn: 肯定式与否定式只差一个否定前缀。

normal.en: The family runs literacy, illiteracy, literature, literal, literary.
normal.cn: 同族包括「读写能力」「文盲状态」「文学」「字面的」「文学的」。

normal.en: The noun use is rare but real, as in counts of literates.
normal.cn: 名词用法少见但真实存在，如统计识字者人数。

abstract.en: Picture a person carrying a bag of letters that opens every official door.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人背着一袋字母，能打开每一扇公务的门。

abstract.en: Picture glasses that turn a page of marks into sentences.
abstract.cn: 想象一副眼镜，把满页符号变成句子。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp kept lit at the same desk for fifty years.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张书桌上点了五十年的灯。

examples.en: A literate population reads instructions and changes behaviour faster.
examples.cn: 识字的人口能更快读懂说明并改变行为。

examples.en: She was literate in three languages before she left school.
examples.cn: 她离开学校前已能用三种语言读写。

examples.en: Any computer-literate volunteer can update the parish register.
examples.cn: 任何会用电脑的志愿者都能更新教区登记册。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里特瑞特」——里面特别认得那些小字，就是识字的。

root: 拉丁 littera「字母」加表「具有」的形容词后缀构成 litteratus「写有字母的、有学问的」，十五世纪进入英语，后扩展指任何能读写的人。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the plain ability to read through cultivation, practical paperwork, computers, specialist fields and style, until the adjective finally names the people themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从最基本的读写能力出发，经过教养、日常文书、电脑、专业领域与文风，最后用这个形容词直接指人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tracing lines of print on a page beside a stack of worn books.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手在页面上顺着印刷字行移动，旁边是一摞翻旧的书。

branches.en: THE BASE: the plain ability to read and write comes first.
branches.cn: 基底：能读能写这一朴素能力排在最前。

branches.en: BOOKS AND BEARERS: reading widely shades into cultivation, and the adjective can name the reader.
branches.cn: 书与读书人：广泛阅读渐成教养，而这个形容词也能直接指读者。

branches.en: PAPERWORK: forms and instructions set a practical threshold for the word.
branches.cn: 文书：表格与说明为这个词设下实用门槛。

branches.en: TOOLS AND FIELDS: screens and specialties each have letters of their own.
branches.cn: 工具与领域：屏幕与专业各自拥有自己的「字母」。

branches.en: STYLE AND SOCIETY: polished prose and a reading public are the word written large.
branches.cn: 文风与社会：打磨过的文字与读书的公众，是这个词的放大形态。

intro.en: The word is a Latin adjective carried into English, built from a noun for a letter and a suffix meaning 'provided with'.
intro.cn: 这是一个直接借入英语的拉丁形容词，由表「字母」的名词与表「被赋予」的后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin littera supplied letter, literature and literal, while the adjective litteratus supplied literate and, with a prefix of denial, illiterate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 littera 衍生出「字母」「文学」与「字面的」，形容词 litteratus 衍生出「识字的」，加上否定前缀则成「不识字的」。

items.example: The noun names the unit a reader must first master.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指读者必须首先掌握的单位。

items.example: The ending turns a possession into a description of a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「拥有某物」变成对人的描述。

items.meaning: provided with letters, able to read
items.example: The witness was literate and signed her own name.
items.exampleCN: 这名证人识字，自己签了名。

items.meaning: the state of being able to read
items.example: Literacy rose sharply after the new school opened.
items.exampleCN: 新学校开办后识字率迅速上升。

items.example: The notice was rewritten for illiterate readers.
items.exampleCN: 这则通知为不识字者重写了一遍。

items.meaning: a sign for a speech sound; a written message
items.example: She wrote the letter in one sitting.
items.exampleCN: 她一口气写完了这封信。

items.example: The magazine reviews literary fiction.
items.exampleCN: 这本杂志评论文学小说。

items.example: The old phrase 'a man of letters' still survives.

definition_zh: 文学；文学作品；文献；资料；宣传印刷品
definition_en: written works such as novels, poems and plays that are valued as art, the books and articles written about a subject, or printed material used to promote something
core_image: 书架上按国别排开的一排小说，书脊颜色深浅不一
scene: 图书馆的旧书区里，一排小说按国别排开，书脊被摸得发亮。She studied English literature at university and later taught it to teenagers.
sceneCN: 这里 literature 是「文学」（第 1 个义项：作为艺术的小说、诗歌与戏剧）；句意为她在大学学习英国文学，后来教青少年。图中可辨识物件：旧书架、按国别排列的小说、发亮的书脊。

pos.zh: 文学；文献；资料；宣传印刷品

derivatives.zh: 与 literature 同出拉丁语 litteratura，义为「文学的；书面的」
由同一词干加 -ate 构成，义为「有读写能力的」
由同一词干加 -cy 构成，义为「读写能力」

senses.title: Written works valued as art
senses.definition: novels, poems, plays and other writing valued for form and imagination rather than for information alone
senses.definitionCN: 小说、诗歌、戏剧等因其形式与想象力而受重视、而非只用来传递信息的写作
senses.example: She studied English literature at university.
senses.exampleCN: 她在大学学习英国文学。
senses.why: Litteratura first meant the act of writing and the learning that letters bring; the works carrying that learning took the name, and artistic writing moved to the centre.
senses.whyCN: litteratura 最初指书写这件事以及文字带来的学问；承载这种学问的作品接过了这个名字，艺术性的写作后来占据了中心。

senses.title: The body of writing on a subject
senses.definition: the books, articles and reports published about a particular subject, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 关于某一主题已出版的书籍、文章与报告的整体
senses.example: The literature on climate change is now enormous.
senses.exampleCN: 关于气候变化的文献现在多得惊人。
senses.why: A subject keeps its knowledge in texts; once those texts pile up, scholars call the whole shelf the literature of the field, even when the writing is technical.
senses.whyCN: 一个学科把知识存放在文本里；文本一旦堆积起来，学者就把整排书架称作该领域的文献，即便那些文字是技术性的。

senses.title: The academic study of literary works
senses.definition: the subject taught and researched at universities that deals with novels, poems and plays
senses.definitionCN: 大学里讲授与研究小说、诗歌、戏剧的学科
senses.example: He teaches literature at a small college.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一所小学规模的学院教文学。
senses.why: A body of texts large enough to be taught turns into a subject; the noun for the works becomes the noun for the department that studies them.
senses.whyCN: 一批文本大到可以被讲授时，就变成了一个学科；指作品的名词于是也用来指研究这些作品的院系。

senses.title: Printed material used for promotion
senses.definition: leaflets, brochures and other printed matter used to advertise or explain something
senses.definitionCN: 用来宣传或说明某事的传单、小册子等印刷品
senses.example: The clinic sent promotional literature to every household.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所给每户人家都寄了宣传资料。
senses.why: Print carries authority, so advertisers borrowed the word for their brochures; a leaflet inherits the seriousness of a book even when it is selling soap.
senses.whyCN: 印刷品自带权威感，于是广告商借这个词来指自己的小册子；一张传单即便在推销肥皂，也继承了书本的严肃。

intro.en: Literature comes from a Latin word for writing and learning, and only later narrowed towards novels, poems and plays.
intro.cn: literature 来自拉丁语中表示书写与学问的词，后来才收窄到指小说、诗歌与戏剧。

items.en: Littera meant a letter of the alphabet, and the plural litterae often meant a written document or a letter sent to someone.
items.cn: littera 指字母表中的一个字母，复数 litterae 常指文书或寄给人的书信。

items.en: Litteratura named writing and the learning gained from letters, but not yet a shelf of novels.
items.cn: litteratura 指书写活动以及由文字得来的学问，那时还不指一整架小说。

items.en: Old French took the word as literature, still meaning learning and written culture rather than fiction.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词写作 literature，仍指学问与书面文化，而不是虚构故事。

items.en: Early English used literature for polite learning and scholarship; the modern sense of imaginative writing developed slowly.
items.cn: 早期英语用 literature 指文雅的学问与学术；指想象性写作的现代义项是慢慢发展出来的。

items.en: Modern English centres literature on novels, poems and plays, while keeping the older sense for the body of writing on any subject.
items.cn: 现代英语把 literature 的中心放在小说、诗歌与戏剧，同时保留较旧的义项，指任何主题的文献整体。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of letters and writing; the near-meaning group gathers words for stories, poems and written work.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中「字母、书写」的词干展开；近义组收表示故事、诗歌与文字作品的词。

entries.definition: Relating to literature or to formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 文学的；书面的；由同一拉丁词干构成。

entries.definition: Able to read and write.
entries.definitionCN: 有读写能力的；来自同一词干。

entries.definition: The ability to read and write.
entries.definitionCN: 读写能力；由同一词干加 -cy 构成。

entries.definition: A written symbol, or a message sent on paper.
entries.definitionCN: 字母；书信；经古法语进入英语，源自拉丁语 littera。

entries.definition: Stories and novels about imagined events.
entries.definitionCN: 虚构作品；讲述想象事件的故事与小说。

entries.definition: Poems as a form of literature.
entries.definitionCN: 诗歌；作为一种文学形式的诗。

entries.definition: Books, articles and other written work.
entries.definitionCN: 著作；文章等书面作品。

entries.definition: Serious academic study and the work it produces.
entries.definitionCN: 学术研究；认真治学及其成果。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of the Latin word for a letter, and its family keeps returning to reading, learning and the works that carry both.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语中表示「字母」的词生长出来，同族词反复回到阅读、学问以及承载二者的作品。

normal.en: Littera is a letter and litteratura is writing made of letters, so literature began as the product of the alphabet.
normal.cn: littera 是字母，litteratura 是由字母写成的文字，所以 literature 最初就是字母的产物。

normal.en: Literature first meant learning gained from books, which is why a literature review still means reading what others have written.
normal.cn: literature 最初指从书本得来的学问，所以文献综述至今仍指阅读别人已经写下的东西。

normal.en: Literary is the adjective and literature the noun: one describes, the other names the whole body of works.
normal.cn: literary 是形容词，literature 是名词：一个作描述，一个指整批作品。

normal.en: A field's literature is the shelf of everything written about it, which is why doctors speak of the literature on a drug.
normal.cn: 一个领域的 literature 就是关于它的全部书面材料，所以医生会说某种药的文献。

normal.en: Promotional literature borrows the prestige of books for leaflets, because print still looks authoritative.
normal.cn: 宣传资料借用了书本的声望来指传单，因为印刷品至今看起来仍然权威。

abstract.en: A library is many voices stored as letters, and literature is the name for that chorus.
abstract.cn: 图书馆是许多声音被存成字母，literature 就是这支合唱的名字。

abstract.en: The same word covers a tragedy and a clinic brochure, because both are printed and meant to be read.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指一部悲剧，也指诊所的小册子，因为两者都是印出来供人阅读的。

abstract.en: Literature is what a culture chooses to keep reading, and that choice changes with each generation.
abstract.cn: 文学是一个文化选择继续阅读的东西，而这个选择会随每一代人改变。

examples.en: She studied English literature at university.
examples.cn: 她在大学学习英国文学。

examples.en: The literature on climate change is now enormous.
examples.cn: 关于气候变化的文献现在多得惊人。

examples.en: The clinic sent promotional literature to every household.
examples.cn: 诊所给每户人家都寄了宣传资料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里头有扯」——书里头有扯不完的故事和道理，literature 就是文学、文献。

root: 拉丁语 littera（字母）→ litteratura（文字写作、由读书得来的学问）→ 古法语 literature → 英语 literature；同族词多与文字、读写、文学有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is letters arranged into works; the senses divide into art writing, the body of texts on a subject, the academic field, and printed promotion.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把字母排成作品；义项由此分出艺术性的写作、某主题的文本整体、学术学科，以及印刷宣传品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf of novels arranged by country, their spines worn bright by handling.
core.cn: 核心意象：书架上按国别排开的一排小说，书脊被翻摸得发亮。

branches.cn: 按国别排列的一架小说

branches.cn: 研讨室里逐行拆解一首诗

intro.cn: 一个表示字母的拉丁词、一个表示书写的拉丁名词、一次法语改写，再加四个英语形式，把 literature 从字母表带到书架与诊所。

latinIntro.cn: littera、litteratura 与 litterarius 都是有记录的拉丁词；其中只有 litteratura 是 literature 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 岩石圈；由地壳与上地幔顶部组成的刚性外壳
definition_en: the rigid outer shell of a planet, made of the crust and the uppermost mantle
core_image: 一颗石球外面套着一层薄而坚硬的石壳，壳上裂成几块大板
scene: 岩石圈并不整体移动，它早已裂成几块大板。The lithosphere is broken into large plates that move slowly over the softer layer below.
sceneCN: 这里 lithosphere 指「岩石圈」（第 1 个义项：地壳与上地幔顶部组成的刚性外壳）；句意为岩石圈裂成几块大板，在下面较软的层之上缓慢移动。

pos.zh: 岩石圈（地壳与上地幔顶部的刚性部分）

senses.title: The rigid outer shell of a planet
senses.titleCN: 岩石圈：行星的刚性外壳
senses.definition: the rigid outer shell of a planet, made of the crust and the uppermost mantle
senses.definitionCN: 由地壳与上地幔顶部组成的行星刚性外壳
senses.example: The lithosphere is broken into large plates that move slowly over the softer layer below.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈裂成几块大板，在下面较软的层之上缓慢移动。
senses.why: The word joins Greek lithos 'stone' with sphaira 'sphere', so it names the stone sphere around a planet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊语 lithos「石头」与 sphaira「球」合在一起，指行星外面那层石头球壳。

senses.title: The layer that carries the plates
senses.definition: the layer whose fragments are the tectonic plates
senses.definitionCN: 其碎块构成构造板块的那一层
senses.example: Each plate is a piece of lithosphere, not a separate sheet of crust.
senses.exampleCN: 每个板块都是岩石圈的一块，而不是单独的一层地壳。
senses.why: Plates are defined mechanically: they are the pieces of the rigid shell, so the shell and the plates are the same material at different scales.
senses.whyCN: 板块是按力学性质界定的：它们是刚性外壳的碎块，所以外壳与板块是同一材料在不同尺度上的说法。

senses.title: Thickness that varies by setting
senses.definition: the part of the shell whose thickness differs under oceans and continents
senses.definitionCN: 这层外壳在海洋之下与大陆之下厚度不同
senses.example: Continental lithosphere can be several times thicker than oceanic lithosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 大陆岩石圈的厚度可以达到大洋岩石圈的好几倍。
senses.why: Old, cold continental roots extend far deeper than young oceanic plates, so the same shell has very different depths.
senses.whyCN: 古老寒冷的大陆根扎得远比年轻的大洋板块深，因此同一层外壳的深度差别很大。

senses.title: Rigid, elastic behaviour
senses.definition: the mechanical property of bending and breaking rather than flowing
senses.definitionCN: 会弯曲、会断裂而不会流动的力学性质
senses.example: The lithosphere bends elastically under the weight of a volcano.
senses.exampleCN: 火山的重压使岩石圈发生弹性弯曲。
senses.why: The key contrast is with the asthenosphere: over long times the shell behaves as a solid, while the layer below can flow.
senses.whyCN: 关键对照是与软流圈的区别：在长时间尺度上这层外壳表现为固体，而下面的层可以流动。

senses.title: The layer above the asthenosphere
senses.definition: the outer shell defined by its position above the weaker asthenosphere
senses.definitionCN: 以位于较软弱的软流圈之上来界定的外壳
senses.example: The boundary between lithosphere and asthenosphere is a change in strength, not in rock type.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈与软流圈的界线是强度的变化，而不是岩石种类的变化。
senses.why: The same rock can belong to either layer; what changes across the boundary is how easily it deforms.
senses.whyCN: 同一种岩石可以属于这两层中的任一层；跨过界线改变的是它变形的难易程度。

senses.title: A planetary shell beyond Earth
senses.titleCN: 地球之外的行星岩石圈
senses.definition: the equivalent rigid shell of another rocky planet or moon
senses.definitionCN: 其他岩石行星或卫星的同类刚性外壳
senses.example: Mars has a thick lithosphere that has barely moved for billions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 火星的岩石圈很厚，数十亿年间几乎没怎么移动。
senses.why: The term is defined by mechanics, so it transfers to any rocky body with a stiff outer layer.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语按力学性质定义，因此可推广到任何具有坚硬外层的岩石天体。

senses.title: The host of resources and earthquakes
senses.definition: the layer in which most mines, oil fields and shallow earthquakes occur
senses.definitionCN: 大多数矿山、油田与浅源地震所在的层
senses.example: Most earthquakes begin within the lithosphere, where rock is brittle enough to break.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数地震始于岩石圈内，那里的岩石足够脆，会断裂。
senses.why: Brittle failure requires a stiff material, so the rigid shell is where faults slip and where resources are dug out.
senses.whyCN: 脆性破坏需要坚硬的材料，因此断层在这层刚性外壳里滑动，资源也从这里开采。

senses.title: The object of lithospheric study
senses.definition: the shell as a subject of geophysics, geochemistry and plate reconstruction
senses.definitionCN: 作为地球物理、地球化学与板块重建研究对象的这层外壳
senses.example: Lithospheric studies combine seismic imaging with heat-flow measurements.
senses.exampleCN: 岩石圈研究把地震成像与热流测量结合起来。
senses.why: Once a layer is named, it becomes a research object with its own methods and its own adjective, lithospheric.
senses.whyCN: 一层一旦被命名，就成为有自己方法和形容词 lithospheric 的研究对象。

intro.en: Lithosphere is a scientific compound coined from two Greek nouns. The parts are transparent and the meaning has stayed stable since the term was formed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: lithosphere 是由两个希腊名词构成的科学复合词。构词成分清楚，术语形成以来含义一直稳定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek lithos meant 'stone', and sphaira meant 'ball, sphere'; both are common in scientific compounds.
items.cn: 希腊语 lithos 意为「石头」，sphaira 意为「球、球体」；两者在科学复合词中都很常见。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geologists needed a name for the solid outer shell of the planet and combined the two Greek nouns.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学家需要给行星的固体外壳命名，就把这两个希腊名词组合起来。

items.en: The English term spread with the growth of geophysics; its modern definition depends on strength, not on chemical composition.
items.cn: 这个英语术语随地球物理的发展而传播；它的现代定义取决于力学强度，而不是化学成分。

items.en: Plate tectonics gave the word a central role: the lithosphere is the layer that breaks into plates and slides over the asthenosphere.
items.cn: 板块构造学说赋予这个词核心地位：岩石圈就是裂成板块并在软流圈上滑动的那一层。

items.en: The paired term asthenosphere was coined later to name the weaker layer below, so the two words are defined against each other.
items.cn: 与之配套的术语 asthenosphere 后来才出现，用来命名下面较软弱的层，因此这两个词是相互对照定义的。

note.en: Group one collects the other -sphere words that are constantly mixed up; group two collects the geological units that sit next to lithosphere in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是极易混淆的其他 -sphere 词；第二组是语义上与岩石圈相邻的地质单位。

entries.definition: the envelope of gases around a planet. It shares the -sphere ending but begins with a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 行星周围的气体层。它共享 -sphere 结尾，但开头是另一个词根。

entries.definition: the zone where living things exist. The first element is Greek bios 'life', not lithos 'stone'.
entries.definitionCN: 生物生存的圈层。前半部分是希腊语 bios「生命」，不是 lithos「石头」。

entries.definition: all the water on a planet. The first element is Greek hydor 'water'.
entries.definitionCN: 行星上的全部水体。前半部分是希腊语 hydor「水」。

entries.definition: a print made by lithography. It shares litho- 'stone' but ends with -graph 'write', not -sphere.
entries.definitionCN: 石版印刷品。它共享 litho-「石头」，但结尾是 -graph「写」，不是 -sphere。

entries.definition: the outermost rocky skin of a planet, thinner than the lithosphere and included within it.
entries.definitionCN: 行星最外面的岩石薄壳，比岩石圈薄，并且包含在岩石圈之内。

entries.definition: one large piece of the lithosphere that moves as a unit.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石圈中作为整体运动的一大块。

entries.definition: the weaker layer beneath the lithosphere, which can flow slowly.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石圈之下较软弱、可以缓慢流动的层。

entries.definition: any outer covering; it describes the shape but carries no geological definition.
entries.definitionCN: 任何外壳；它只描述形状，不含地质学定义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek roots and real layer names, so each word can be decoded rather than merely rhymed.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根与真实的圈层名称，因此每个词可以拆解，而不是只靠押韵。

normal.en: litho- means stone and -sphere means ball, so lithosphere is the stone ball around a planet.
normal.cn: litho- 表示石头，-sphere 表示球，所以 lithosphere 就是行星外面那层石头球壳。

normal.en: The four -sphere words form a set: atmosphere is air, hydrosphere is water, biosphere is life, lithosphere is stone.
normal.cn: 四个 -sphere 词构成一组：atmosphere 是气，hydrosphere 是水，biosphere 是生命，lithosphere 是石头。

normal.en: The lithosphere is the plate itself; the crust is only its top layer, so a plate is thicker than a crust.
normal.cn: 岩石圈就是板块本身；地壳只是它的最上层，所以板块比地壳厚。

normal.en: The boundary with the asthenosphere is a strength boundary, not a rock-type boundary.
normal.cn: 与软流圈的界线是强度界线，不是岩石种类界线。

normal.en: Earthquakes and mines cluster in the lithosphere because brittle rock breaks and holds ore.
normal.cn: 地震与矿山集中在岩石圈，因为脆性岩石会断裂，也能储存矿石。

abstract.en: Abstractly, the lithosphere is a cracked eggshell: hard, thin, and divided into pieces that can slide.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，岩石圈像一层裂开的蛋壳：坚硬、很薄，并分成可以滑动的碎块。

abstract.en: The image pairs hardness with thinness: what makes it a plate is that it can break rather than flow.
abstract.cn: 这个形象把「硬」与「薄」配在一起：使它成为板块的，正是它会断裂而不是流动。

abstract.en: Symbol: a thin hard ring around a soft inner circle, with cracks across the ring.
abstract.cn: 符号：软内圈外面套一层薄硬的环，环上布满裂缝。

examples.en: Oceanic lithosphere is created at mid-ocean ridges and destroyed at trenches.
examples.cn: 大洋岩石圈在大洋中脊生成，在海沟处消亡。

examples.en: The lithosphere behaves as a rigid plate over long time spans.
examples.cn: 在长时间尺度上，岩石圈表现为刚性板块。

examples.en: Scientists map the base of the lithosphere using seismic waves.
examples.cn: 科学家用地震波绘制岩石圈的底部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里索斯菲尔」—— 石头（litho）做的球（sphere） → lithosphere 岩石圈

root: 由希腊语 lithos（石头）与 sphaira（球）组合而成，字面义为「石头球壳」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of lithosphere. The thread is a hard outer shell: it carries the plates, bends elastically, and sits on a softer layer.
sensesIntro.cn: lithosphere 的八个义项。主线是一层坚硬外壳：它承载板块、发生弹性弯曲，并坐在较软的层之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin hard shell around a soft interior, cracked into moving pieces.
core.cn: 核心意象：软内部外面一层薄硬壳，壳裂成会移动的碎块。

branches.en: SHELL AND THICKNESS: the same hard shell is thin under oceans and thick under old continents.
branches.cn: 外壳与厚度：同一层硬壳在海洋下很薄，在古老大陆下很厚。

branches.en: PLATE IDENTITY: a plate is not a separate crust but a fragment of this shell.
branches.cn: 板块同一性：板块不是另一层地壳，而是这层外壳的碎块。

branches.en: STRENGTH BOUNDARY: rigidity is measured against the softer layer below.
branches.cn: 强度界线：刚性是相对于下面较软的层来衡量的。

branches.en: PLANETARY TRANSFER: the mechanical definition works on any rocky body.
branches.cn: 行星推广：这一定义按力学性质成立，因此适用于任何岩石天体。

branches.en: HUMAN USE: the same shell holds ore, breaks in earthquakes and becomes an object of study.
branches.cn: 人类利用：同一层外壳储存矿石、在地震中破裂，也成为研究对象。

intro.en: Lithosphere is a compound of two Greek nouns, and both parts recur across scientific English, so the word is easy to decode and easy to extend.
intro.cn: lithosphere 由两个希腊名词复合而成，两部分在科学英语中反复出现，因此这个词既好拆解也便于扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: the elements are Greek lithos and sphaira, combined in modern scientific coinage, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源：构词成分是希腊语 lithos 与 sphaira，在现代科技术语中组合而成，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: Lithology is the study of rock types.
The atmosphere is the gaseous sphere of a planet.
items.exampleCN: 大气层是行星的气体圈层。

items.meaningCN: 与岩石圈有关的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: Lithospheric plates move a few centimetres a year.
items.exampleCN: 岩石圈板块每年移动几厘米。

items.meaningCN: 岩石类型研究（-logy 表示学科）
items.example: The drill core changed lithology at two hundred metres.
items.exampleCN: 钻芯在两百米处岩性发生变化。

items.meaningCN: 使沉积物变成岩石（-ify 表示使成为）
items.example: Pressure and cementation lithify loose sand.
items.exampleCN: 压力与胶结作用把松砂变成岩石。

items.meaning: made of stone; relating to stone
items.example: Archaeologists found lithic tools in the cave.
items.exampleCN: 考古学家在洞中发现了石制工具。

items.meaning: a rigid fragment of the lithosphere
items.meaningCN: 岩石圈的一块刚性碎块
items.example: Each lithosphere plate carries both crust and upper mantle.
items.exampleCN: 每个岩石圈板块都带着地壳与上地幔。

items.meaning: the depth where the rigid shell meets the weaker layer
items.meaningCN: 刚性外壳与较软层相接的深度（复合术语）
items.example: The lithosphere-asthenosphere boundary lies near one hundred kilometres under oceans.
items.exampleCN: 大洋之下的岩石圈与软流圈界面约在一百公里深处。
